title: 'Lioness' star Jill Wagner raises daughters in Tennessee town of 800, where horses and buggies still roam
summary: "A Very Arctic Christmas" and "Lioness" star Jill Wagner traded Hollywood for a Tennessee town of 800, where Mennonites ride horses and buggies.
story: "A Very Arctic Christmas" star tells Fox News Digital why she traded Hollywood's fast pace for small-town Tennessee and the life lessons she hopes her daughters will carry into adulthood.
From the high-stakes action of "Lioness" to the holiday adventure of "A Very Arctic Christmas," Jill Wagner is taking on two very different worlds.

But off camera, the actress has traded Hollywood's hustle for a quieter life raising her two daughters on a Tennessee farm in a town of just 800 people — where horses and buggies are still a familiar sight.
"First of all, I love Tennessee … I'm from the South. I'm from North Carolina," she told Fox News Digital. "I love the people here but especially love the small-town mentality."
'RANSOM CANYON' STAR JOSH DUHAMEL SAYS HE'D RATHER PUT MONEY INTO NORTH DAKOTA AFTER SELLING LOS ANGELES HOME
Life in her Tennessee town offers a glimpse of a world that can feel far removed from Hollywood.
Jill Wagner reunites with Cameron Mathison in "A Very Arctic Christmas," bringing her signature holiday charm. (Great American Media)
"I was at the post office this morning and one of the Mennonites was in front of me … I got to look at their horse and buggy," she said.
Wagner said the small-town atmosphere has become an important part of the childhood she and her husband want to give their girls.
The actress explained why she hopes her daughters will eventually appreciate the slower pace, even if they someday follow in her footsteps and move to bigger cities.
WATCH: JILL WAGNER TRADES HOLLYWOOD HUSTLE FOR TENNESSEE FAMILY LIFE
"In some ways, going back to a simpler, slower pace … I think as we get older, or at least I know I can speak for myself, as I get older, I really value that," she added.
Wagner knows the pull of Hollywood firsthand. She left home at 17 to pursue a career in entertainment and suspects her daughters may one day be eager to spread their own wings.
But she hopes they'll always remember what their upbringing gave them.
‘SOPRANOS’ STAR JAMIE-LYNN SIGLER FLED HOLLYWOOD FOR TEXAS WHERE SHE NO LONGER FEELS ‘WATCHED’

"And I'm sure they'll do the same, but I hope what it does is bring them back to the simple-ness of life and what it can be … That's a gift that my husband and I gave them, and they probably don't even know it yet," she said.
Jill Wagner and Cameron Mathison stand together at a wildlife rehabilitation facility decorated for Christmas for the film, "A Very Arctic Christmas." (Great American Media)
Away from the action of "Lioness," Wagner is embracing the holiday spirit in "A Very Arctic Christmas," reuniting with Cameron Mathison for a festive adventure.
Wagner plays Jane, a wildlife conservationist who helps a father and daughter navigate an unexpected Arctic adventure after their holiday cruise goes off course.
"Lioness" star Jill Wagner says raising her daughters with small-town values is a gift they may not fully appreciate until they're older. (Lauren Smith/Paramount+)
The actress said working with Mathison brings plenty of laughs to "A Very Arctic Christmas" set.

"There's never any dull moment when you have Cameron Mathison and I on set together. In fact, it's hard for us to get through a scene without laughing, I'm sure. Robin Dunne, the director, is always rolling his eyes, like, ‘Oh, guys, guys, guys, guys, bring it in,'" she laughed.
WATCH: JILL WAGNER DISHES ON THE ON-SET CHAOS WITH CO-STAR CAMERON MATHISON
For Wagner, the holiday films also have a personal connection.
The actress has found ways to include her daughters in her Christmas-movie tradition.
When Wagner's daughters were younger, she included them in one of her films as extras, giving them a chance to sit on Santa's lap.
Now that they're older, Wagner said they understand that Christmas movies are a genre of their own — and she hopes the experience becomes a lasting family tradition.

"And I just hope that one day when I'm long and gone, that is a tradition with each other's families is that they get on Christmas, and they get to watch that movie and just kind of laugh at the fact that we're all in a movie together at Christmas," she added.

While Wagner's career continues to take her between intense action roles and feel-good holiday projects, she values sharing those experiences with her daughters while giving them a childhood rooted in small-town life.
Jill Wagner and husband David Lemanowicz kissing at the "Lioness" Season 2 premiere. (Variety via Getty Images)
When Fox News Digital asked whether her daughters were becoming the Tennessee farm girls she had envisioned, Wagner admitted there's still some work to do.
"So, I don't know about farm girl. I know that … they love outdoors. They don't necessarily like doing farm work. So, we're trying to still work on that," she laughed.
"They do love running around barefooted in the dirt, and they can play outside all day long, which I love for them," Wagner said.
The family hopes to add chickens and goats when Wagner's work schedule allows more time at home.
"Maybe one day we'll get a horse or a pony for them," she added.

"Lioness" star Jill Wagner says raising her daughters with small-town values is a gift they may not fully appreciate until they're older. (John Nacion/Variety via Getty Images)
But for Wagner, the biggest perk of small-town life isn't just the farm — it's the neighbors who show up when it matters.

Her family owns Scott Mansion Farms, where they host charitable events benefiting the Special Operations Warrior Foundation and Dolly Parton's Children's Hospital. Wagner said the community's support has been especially meaningful.

"But the fact that people just show up at the gate and say, ‘What can we do to help?’ I think it just reminds me of how amazing humanity is … and how very special it is to have good neighbors," she said.
Wagner also hopes her daughters inherit her love of local festivals and community traditions.

"It's woven into my fabric. So, I'm going to pass that on to my girls. Hopefully they'll have the love for that like I do," she said.

title: Buckingham Palace 'blindsided' by Thomas Markle allegations as Harry, Meghan face new family turmoil: expert
summary: Buckingham Palace was reportedly "blindsided" by disturbing allegations involving Meghan Markle's estranged father, Thomas Markle, now under investigation.
story: Royal commentator Kinsey Schofield says Buckingham Palace was blindsided by allegations involving Meghan Markle's father, Thomas Markle Sr., who denies the claims.
Buckingham Palace was reportedly "blindsided" by allegations involving Meghan Markle's estranged father, former Hollywood lighting director Thomas Markle Sr.

The Sun reported on Oct. 22 that Thomas Markle Jr. said he found "hundreds, if not thousands" of images depicting child sexual abuse while clearing out boxes at his father's former home in Cebu, Philippines. Markle Jr. told the newspaper that he reported the images to Philippine police and contacted the FBI in the U.S.

The 82-year-old Markle denied the allegations to the Daily Mail, telling the newspaper: "I'm shocked, I'm hurt, and I'm very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I'm being accused of. It's the worst thing anyone could accuse me of."
PRINCE HARRY MAKING 'BIG MISTAKE' THAT COULD DESTROY CHANCE OF ROYAL RECONCILIATION: EXPERT
Meghan Markle allegedly protected her two kids from her father, Thomas Markle Sr. (Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Markle Sr. for comment.

"Following the report, I made more than 40 phone calls to royal sources over the weekend, and nobody I spoke to had heard anything about these allegations before the story broke in The Sun," Kinsey Schofield, host of the YouTube show "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital.
Meghan Markle said her decision to distance herself was intended to protect her children. (Getty Images)
"My understanding is that Buckingham Palace was blindsided," she said. "They find themselves dragged into another controversy involving [the Sussexes]. And the allegations are deeply disturbing."
WATCH: BUCKINGHAM PALACE WAS 'BLINDSIDED' BY THOMAS MARKLE SR. ALLEGATIONS: EXPERT
Fox News Digital reached out to Buckingham Palace for comment.

In a statement sent to Fox News Digital, Meghan wrote: "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed. In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father, and I was given assurances that these were being investigated."

The Sun reported that Thomas Markle Jr. recently found "hundreds, if not thousands" of images depicting child sexual abuse in boxes at his father’s former home in the Philippine city of Cebu when he was clearing out the property. (Getty Images)

"I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them," she wrote. "I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.

"Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children."
WATCH: KING CHARLES MAY PRIVATELY SUPPORT MEGHAN MARKLE AMID CONTROVERSY: EXPERT

The Metropolitan Police said its records show that the letter was received in January 2019, not 2018. Meghan's spokesperson subsequently acknowledged the discrepancy, saying the police's timestamped records should be treated as authoritative.

The letter was written by Markle Sr.'s first wife, Roslyn Markle, also known as Roslyn Loveless, ITV News reported on Oct. 26. The outlet said it had reviewed the letter, which contained allegations of sexual abuse against Markle Sr. He has denied the allegations.
Thomas Markle Sr. has denied the allegations. (GC Images)

Melvin Matibag, director of the Philippines' National Bureau of Investigation, told The Associated Press that the FBI had requested the bureau's assistance in investigating Markle Jr.'s allegations against his father.
Thomas Markle Sr. is 82. (GC Images)
Philippine Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla separately told the AP that the Philippine National Police was also investigating Markle Jr.'s allegations against his father. Remulla did not elaborate.
A spokesperson for Remulla told Fox News Digital that the Philippine National Police (PNP) is continuing its investigation.
Members of the British royal family, including Prince William, are keeping their distance. (Getty Images)
Schofield said the royal family would likely keep its distance from the Sussexes as its members prioritize their duties while the investigation continues.

King Charles III and Queen Camilla attend a commemoration event at Aberfan Memorial Garden to mark the 60th anniversary of the Aberfan disaster on Oct. 21, 2026, in Merthyr Tydfil, Wales. (Getty Images)

"King Charles is in a difficult position," said Schofield. "As a father, I believe he would want to offer Harry emotional support. Let's not forget, it was the king who walked Meghan down the aisle when her own father couldn't. But Harry has repeatedly shared private conversations through interviews, documentaries and his memoir. The king would be reluctant to have a sensitive conversation on this topic with Prince Harry without reassurance that it would remain private."
The royals are expected to keep calm and carry on with their duties. (Getty Images)

"As for Prince William, don't expect him to get involved," said Schofield. "This is not his fight. The palace has already established that Harry and Meghan are private citizens who do not represent the crown. This is a matter for the Sussex household. The Metropolitan Police have confirmed that allegations were passed to Sussex's office in 2019, but the police say they did not share those allegations with other law enforcement agencies. My royal sources have given me no indication that the palace was informed."

"Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children," Meghan Markle said in a statement. A spokesperson for London's Metropolitan Police told Fox News Digital: "Following a thorough review of Met Police systems and records, we have confirmed that in January 2019, we received a letter containing a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom. It was sent to the MPS Protection Command to raise concerns in relation to the security of the Duchess of Sussex."
Thomas Markle Jr. allegedly found his father in possession of child pornographic material, including photos and videos. (Getty Images)

"The letter was reviewed, and a decision was made that it should be passed to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness," the statement said. "The details of the allegations in the letter were not shared with other law enforcement agencies. The MPS is reviewing the handling of this matter in 2019 and considering whether a referral to the IOPC is necessary to review our approach."

Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, and Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, arrive at The Community Recording Studio, a youth and community charity, during their visit to Nottingham on Oct. 15, 2026, in Nottingham, England. (Getty Images)

The Metropolitan Police's review concerns how the force handled the letter in 2019, rather than a criminal investigation into Markle Sr. British police said they were also considering whether to refer their handling of the matter to the Independent Office for Police Conduct, the police watchdog in England and Wales.

The Times reported that the Metropolitan Police shared the information with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, but apparently not with other members of the royal household. Buckingham Palace declined to comment to the newspaper.

According to the outlet, Scotland Yard said the letter contained several allegations of offenses outside the United Kingdom, but police did not launch an investigation at the time. The force acknowledged that it had not shared the allegations with overseas authorities.
Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital that although the king might privately offer support to the Sussexes, he is unlikely to comment publicly on the investigation.
King Charles is seen here with his heir, Prince William. (Aaron Chown - WPA Pool/Getty Images)

"He cannot publicly be seen to be doing anything at all," said Turner. "Neither can any of the members of the royal family because of this potential investigation. According to the prosecutor in Cebu in the Philippines, quick decisions are going to be made."
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is on holiday with her husband and their two children. (Getty Images)
"What I see is Meghan, again, right in the middle of a controversy that is not of her doing," he said.
British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital that her sources were not commenting because "this is being treated as a private Sussex matter."

Prince Harry looks at his bride, Meghan Markle, as she arrives with then-Prince Charles during their wedding in St. George's Chapel at Windsor Castle on May 19, 2018, in Windsor, England. (Getty Images)

"To date, while there has been no formal comment, needless to say, there's nothing about this the royals would want to be associated with," said Fordwich. "It is extremely unlikely the king, or any royal, comments in any way regarding the gravity of these allegations. Institutional distancing is more than likely."

People magazine reported that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex were receiving updates on the allegations while vacationing with their two children during a school break.
"It's been really difficult," a friend told the outlet. "[Meghan's] really cut up. She has young children, and I think that, alongside the victims, it's just weighing on her mind. It's traumatic."
Meghan Markle is a mom to Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5. (2025 Getty Images)
There is also "a slight sense of relief that this is all coming out," the friend said, adding that Meghan hopes "a proper investigation can take place."
A source told People magazine that Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, feels a sense of relief that the news has come to light. (Getty Images)

A source close to Meghan told People magazine: "There is a lot to process emotionally. But she's doing okay. She's holding up. She's surrounded by loved ones and is feeling supported right now. She has great people around her getting through this moment."
On Oct. 24, The Sun reported that Meghan sent her father a letter in December 2025 while he was recovering in a Philippine hospital from a leg amputation following a blood clot.
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex recently relocated to the U.K. (Chris Jackson - Pool/Getty Images)

According to the newspaper, Meghan wrote that she was aware of the sexual abuse allegations against Markle Sr. and would never allow him to meet her two children. She also reportedly told him it would be the last time he heard from her.
Meghan Markle reportedly told Thomas Markle Sr. that he will never meet her children. (Jonathan Brady-Pool/Getty Images)
The outlet reported that Meghan arranged for hospital staff to deliver the letter to her father's bedside, ask him to sign a form acknowledging receipt and record his acceptance of the letter.

Markle Sr. is receiving care at a rehabilitation center in Florida, People magazine reported.

title: Amy Grant says Vince Gill isn't 'afraid to put somebody in their place' after confronting radio host
summary: Amy Grant describes how Vince Gill once threatened to kick Don Imus' butt on air for mocking their marriage, turning a feud into friendship.
story: Amy Grant recalls how a chance doctor visit saved her life. The singer was diagnosed with a potentially catastrophic heart condition after  accompanying husband Vince Gill to his cardiologist appointment.
Amy Grant is opening up about her relationship with her husband, Vince Gill, after over 20 years of marriage, saying he will always stand up for her.
During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 65-year-old singer touched on her marriage to Gill, noting that while he is "kind, kind, kind," he will do anything to protect her.

"He does have a toggle switch, and if somebody does something to throw that switch, he can respond so quickly," she said. "And so he can see the field, and he's got a quick mind. And he is not afraid to put somebody in their place or be protective. And so, yeah, I mean, I feel so loved by him."
In March, Gill told the story of the time he confronted host Don Imus while on his radio show, and called him out for talking negatively about him and Grant.
Grant shared that Gill is not afraid to stand up for her, no matter who he is going up against. (John Shearer/Getty Images for CMT)
AMY GRANT'S EMOTIONAL ACCOUNT OF DOCTORS AND NURSES SINGING OUTSIDE DOLLY PARTON'S HOSPITAL ROOM

He told the "Naked Lunch" podcast that Imus started out as a fan of his, but after he married Grant the radio host changed his tune and would say things such as, "Vince Gill, lost the Baby Jesus, married that Christian girl." While on his radio show, Gill waited until Grant's name came up and then took his chance to stand up for his wife.

"I said, ‘Well, if you ever met her, you'd never say an unkind word about her,’" Gill said. "‘I'm going to shoot you straight.’ I said, ‘I really only came on this show for one reason.’ I said, ‘We're either going to talk this out, straighten this out,’ I said, 'or I'm going to crawl across this desk, and I'm going to kick your a--.'"
Vince Gill threatened to beat Imus up if he continued to speak poorly of his wife. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

Gill noted that on his way home from the interview, he caught Imus on the air and heard him say, "I don't know why I was giving that guy so much crap. I love that guy," adding that the two of them stayed friends until Imus' death in December 2019.

When speaking with Fox News Digital, Grant described all the ways Gill has shown up for her throughout their marriage, including when she had unexpected open-heart surgery in 2020, and when she had a bike accident in 2022, which affected her short-term memory.

Grant credits Gill for being there for her through all her struggles, including after her bike accident. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)

"My short-term memory was shot. There's so much I couldn't remember," she recalled. "I was processing so slow and I just remember saying to him, 'What if this is all I ever had? What if this is as good as it gets?' And he said, 'Amy, anything could happen to any of us. An accomplished musician could have a stroke and never use their left hand again.' And he said, 'We're just going to take each day and it's enough.'"
She explained that his message of staying together no matter what, is something he has always conveyed, "whether spoken or not."

"We've just discovered each other day by day over 26 years and I love him more now. The more I know him, the more I love him. And everybody's life partner is just their life partner. And so you just get to know each other at every new chapter and life brings a lot to everybody."
Grant and Gill welcomed their daughter, Corrina, in March 2001. (Taylor Hill/WireImage)

Gill and Grant married in March 2000 and welcomed their daughter, Corrina, in March 2001. They met in 1993 while both married to other people. They confirmed they were dating in October 1999. After Gill and his first wife divorced in 1997, Grant and her first husband separated in 1998.

title: Collin Gosselin calls out reality TV producers for putting ratings ahead of kids: 'The show must go on'
summary: Collin Gosselin's memoir alleges child exploitation on "Jon & Kate Plus 8," claiming production priorities came at the expense of his well-being.
story: The "Jon & Kate Plus 8" star tells Fox News Digital reality TV puts children at risk when adults ignore their discomfort.
Collin Gosselin is sounding the alarm on the reality TV industry, accusing adults of turning a blind eye when children are hurting — all to keep the cameras rolling.

The "Jon & Kate Plus 8" star is revisiting the painful realities of his youth in his new memoir, "In the Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood," alleging that what made for compelling television often came at the expense of the children living it.
"It's the simple fact that adults that are seeing these things, they surely understood that people are choosing not to say anything because the show must go on," Collin told Fox News Digital.
'JON & KATE PLUS 8' STAR COLLIN GOSSELIN ACCUSES MOM OF TRYING TO 'BURY' HIM TO 'PROTECT HER REPUTATION'
Kate continued filming with her children following her split from Jon Gosselin. (Donna Svennevik/Disney General Entertainment Content)
"And if, at any point in time, a child can voice that they do not want to film, we need to take that seriously," he said.

Collin, one of the sextuplets who rose to fame alongside his parents and siblings, said children should not have to clearly articulate their distress before the adults around them recognize something is wrong.

"To understand and to know that at a young age, at any age, means that you really, you feel in your heart that it is not right, and you know you're being exploited and that's crazy for a child to know," he said. "But we should listen to that because that's a huge thing."
WATCH HERE: COLLIN GOSSELIN CALLS OUT REALITY TV PRODUCERS FOR PUTTING RATINGS AHEAD OF KIDS

Collin Gosselin says growing up in front of reality TV cameras came at an emotional cost, alleging that warning signs were ignored to keep filming. (Donna Svennevik/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images, Brad Barket/WireImage for Discovery Communications)
Even when children remain silent, Collin argued, adults have a responsibility to pay attention.

"But even without a child saying anything, you can tell, you can absolutely tell. It's reading body language," Collin said. "You can absolutely tell and we should be aware. We should be paying attention. We should be protecting children."
WATCH: COLLIN GOSSELIN BLASTS MOM KATE FOR 'BURYING' HIM TO SAVE HER REPUTATION
Collin said the show's production priorities came at the expense of his well-being and that of his siblings, arguing that the demands of filming conflicted with what was best for the children.

"100% my entire childhood, what was best for production was this direct relationship to what was unhealthy for a child," he said. "But nobody cared about the welfare of me and my siblings, they cared about my paycheck."
He also said his siblings were kept in the dark about what happened at home while they were at school, adding that he hopes they will examine his account for themselves.
JON GOSSELIN CLAIMS HE'S 'PERFECT STRANGERS NOW' WITH SIX OF HIS KIDS AFTER YEARS OF NO CONTACT
"A lot happened that was kept from them intentionally so that they could be told that their brother was this and that," Collin said.
As filming intensified, Collin said the family's public image took priority over the children's experiences at home.
Left to right are sextuplet twins Aaden J Gosselin, Leah H Gosselin, Collin T Gosselin, Joel K Gosselin, Alexis F Gosselin and Hannah J Gosselin. (MediaNews Group/Reading Eagle via Getty Images)

"But once everything got going, and we were at the height of filming and production, it was absolutely more about what it looked like on the outside and not necessarily how me and my siblings felt," he said. "It was always about how it looked for everybody else."
For Collin, the failure is not simply recognizing that something is wrong, but refusing to act.
"Doing something about it because the biggest thing is when we know something's wrong, and we don't say anything that's worse than not knowing it," he said.
Collin said the family that audiences watched on "Jon & Kate Plus 8" did not reflect the full reality of his childhood, arguing that viewers saw a more polished version of life at home.
KATE GOSSELIN CALLED A 'MONSTER' IN SOCIAL MEDIA COMMENTS AFTER SON COLLIN ANNOUNCES MEMOIR
When asked what cameras failed to capture, he described experiences and opportunities that he said were offered to the children for filming but later taken away.

His criticism goes beyond editing and production decisions. Collin also revisited his experience of being placed in a treatment facility and given medication, describing a period when he felt stripped of control over his life.

"For a long time, my name was dragged, and I was put away. I was essentially put in a juvenile prison, put on all these medications," he said. "I was a zombie half the time. I had no control, I had nothing."
WATCH: COLLIN GOSSELIN DETAILS ALLEGED ABUSE, CONFRONTS FAMILY TRAUMA
He said he spent that time doing what he was told, with little ability to change his circumstances.
"I did what I was told. I went through the motions, and was like a zombie every day," he said.
Reflecting on that experience, Collin said he feels compelled to speak publicly about what happened.
"And so when you reflect on all that, you realize these things need to be talked about, and I feel just an urge to talk about them," he said.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Collin said he has not spoken to his mother. He recalled a visit from Kate when he was 13, claiming the encounter left him with a painful final memory.
"She berated me for all of 20 minutes after not seeing me for over a year," he said.
Meanwhile, Collin told Fox News Digital he held on to hope even during what he described as his darkest moments.
Collin Gosselin is speaking out about his childhood on "Jon & Kate Plus 8," accusing adults behind the scenes of prioritizing production over children's well-being. (Getty Images)
"I had very little hope, but I always had some, and I hung on to that … I just kept telling myself that there's a better future for me and there will be a time where I will be past this," he said.
The former child star said sharing his story had weighed on him for years before he finally decided to speak publicly.
"It was heavy on my heart to tell my story and to hope that it would create change," he said.
As for reconciliation with his mother, Collin said an apology alone would not be enough to repair their relationship.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Collin opened up about his alleged abuse in his new memoir, "In the Shadow of Eight." (Michael Simon/Getty Images)

"Reconciliation requires action and accountability," he said. "I think we can all say, I'm sorry, but if we're not willing to take the actions and take accountability for what has happened in the past and what happened my entire childhood, then what does that really mean, you know?"
"Jon & Kate Plus 8" followed Jon and Kate Gosselin as they raised their twin daughters, Mady and Cara, alongside their sextuplets: Collin, Alexis, Hannah, Aaden, Leah and Joel.

The series aired from 2007 to 2009 before returning as "Kate Plus 8" in 2010. Following the couple's divorce, Collin was placed in a treatment facility as a child. He later moved in with his father, Jon Gosselin, after Jon obtained custody.

title: Macklemore called 'out of touch' over speech at Free Palestine Tour kickoff
summary: Macklemore launched his Free Palestine Tour in Dublin with defiant remarks about his removal from Ed Sheeran's lineup, sparking mixed reactions.
story: Former Israeli special envoy Noa Tishby discusses rising antisemitism in America, the fallout from the Macklemore-Ed Sheeran controversy and more on ‘My View with Lara Trump.’
Macklemore took his political message to a new stage.
The rapper doubled down on his pro-Palestinian activism during the launch of his Free Palestine Tour, weeks after his controversial remarks prompted his removal from Ed Sheeran's lineup.

"I ​am proud to stand here on stage in solidarity with the Palestinian people. We will ​continue to fight for collective liberation until our last breath," Macklemore told the crowd during his concert in Dublin, according to Reuters.
"Six weeks ago, two words is all ​that it took," he said, referring to the fallout after he declared "Free Palestine" while opening for Ed Sheeran.

Macklemore doubled down on his "Free Palestine" remarks during the opening of his tour. (Zoe Rain/Reuters)

"Those two words are so threatening to some people that we'd rather silence those two words than confront what they ​actually mean. ... Somehow those words have become more controversial than the suffering that made them necessary," Macklemore added.

Macklemore's defiant remarks drew mixed reactions online, with some social media users applauding his outspoken activism while others questioned his motives and accused him of being out of touch. Critics also took aim at the rapper's priorities, suggesting he should focus his attention on problems closer to home rather than delivering political speeches onstage.

"The past few years have taken me through fires I never imagined I’d have to walk through. Seasons of heartbreak, loss, and moments when I didn’t know if I would ever make it to the other side. I wondered if I would ever find my forever … if I would ever feel safe enough to truly breathe again," she continued.
"And then God sent me J. Right in the middle of the heartbreak. Before all the pieces were put back together. And somehow, he began healing parts of me he never broke.
The 29-year-old reality star defended her "huge" age gap with her partner, Jason.  (Kat Ramirez for Fox News Digital)
"My protector. My fiercest fighter. My most loyal person. My lover. My safe place. A man with the patience of Job — and Lord knows he needs it. The one who makes me laugh even on my hardest days.
"For the first time in a long time, I feel safe. I feel fulfilled. I can finally exhale. I found my forever in you."
Chrisley went on to describe her pregnancy as the couple’s "sweetest blessing yet."
"J, watching the way you already love and protect our baby before he/she has even entered this world has made me fall in love with you in an entirely new way," she wrote.

"Not a single doctor’s appointment missed. Constantly caring for me, talking about our baby, and reminding me how beautiful my growing bump is. I thank God every day that this baby gets to call you Daddy."
Chrisley also addressed women who may be waiting for their own "forever."
"And to the woman still in her waiting season… wondering when it will finally be her turn, wondering if God has forgotten her… Please don’t mistake God’s silence for His absence," she wrote.
"Sometimes He’s writing the most beautiful chapters of your story while you’re still trying to make sense of the ones that broke your heart.
"I once prayed just to make it through another day. Now I get to spend forever with the love of my life, carrying a little miracle we already love more than words," she continued.
"From heartbreak to healing. From surviving to living. From praying for my forever to building a family with him.
Chrisley announced her pregnancy Tuesday.  (George Walker IV/AP Photo)
"Only God could have written this story."

Chrisley previously discussed her relationship with Jason during a June appearance on the "Whine Down with Jana Kramer" podcast, where she admitted that her father, Todd Chrisley, is "not too fond" of the age difference.
"Age-gap relationships are the new thing. You’re going to see it everywhere," she said. "There are all these couples that are huge age-gap relationships, but it just works. It’s insane.
"For me, I’m not dealing with the insecurity of a younger guy who’s trying to keep up. Honestly, it’s the healthiest relationship I’ve ever been in," she continued.

"First off, he does way better than I do. And I love that because I’m like, ‘You’re not intimidated by me. You think what I do is great. You don’t try to stifle me.’"

title: ‘Kate & Allie’ star Susan Saint James dead at 80
summary: Susan Saint James, beloved star of "McMillan & Wife" and "Kate & Allie," died Monday at 80 after a battle with pancreatic cancer, People reported.
story: A video obituary courtesy of the Associated Press looks back at Susan Saint James’ career, including her roles in "McMillan & Wife" and "Kate & Allie."
Susan Saint James, the actress known for "McMillan & Wife" and "Kate & Allie," has died.
Saint James, 80, died Monday after a battle with pancreatic cancer, People magazine reported.

"She never met a stranger. Every person she met became the most important person in the room at that moment, from a fellow board member to the clerk at the shoe store, who usually walked away knowing her entire life story," a representative told People.

"Her defining act: weeks after losing her youngest son, Teddy, in the November 28, 2004 plane crash, she delivered his eulogy as a note to each of her other children and her husband, giving them words to heal. Even in the deepest grief of her life, she put everyone else first. Days after the crash she sat with Tim Russert to thank the people who had reached out and to tell them the family was okay."
HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026
She won a Primetime Emmy Award in 1969 for her role as Peggy Maxwell on "The Name of the Game." (Charley Gallay/Getty Images)
Susan Saint James died Monday at 80 after a battle with pancreatic cancer. (CBS/Getty Images)
"She brought that same fire and positivity to everything that followed, and never lost it," the statement continued.

Saint James began her career modeling before switching gears to television. Her breakthrough came in 1968 when she landed the role of research assistant Peggy Maxwell on NBC's "The Name of the Game." Her performance earned her a Primetime Emmy Award in 1969 and established her as one of television's rising stars.
She earned her biggest fame as Sally McMillan, the plucky wife of Rock Hudson’s San Francisco police commissioner Stewart McMillan, in the hit series "McMillan & Wife" from 1971-1976.
Susan Saint James starred as Sally McMillan on "McMillan & Wife" from 1971 to 1976. (NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
She left the NBC show before its sixth and final season because of a contract dispute, with her character killed off in a plane crash.
Saint James later found renewed success alongside Jane Curtin in the popular CBS sitcom "Kate & Allie," which ran from 1984 to 1989.
She is also known for roles in "Love at First Bite," "How to Beat the High Cost of Living," "M*A*S*H," "Law & Order: SVU" and "Suits."
Susan Saint James co-starred with Jane Curtin on the CBS sitcom "Kate & Allie," which ran from 1984 to 1989. (CBS Photo Archive/Getty Images)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Offscreen, Saint James was married to longtime NBC executive and former "Saturday Night Live" producer Dick Ebersol, whom she met while hosting the comedy show in 1981. The family suffered a devastating tragedy in 2004 when their 14-year-old son, Teddy, died in a private plane crash in Colorado.
She was previously married to Richard Neubert and makeup artist Tom Lucas.
Susan Saint James and her husband, Dick Ebersol, lost their 14-year-old son, Teddy, in a 2004 private plane crash. (Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Saint James is survived by her husband, her four children – Sunshine Lucas, Harmony Lucas, Charlie Ebersol and Willie Ebersol – her seven grandchildren, and her sister, Mary Mercedes Dewey.
She is also survived by her beloved service dog, Lola.
After "Kate & Allie" ended, Saint James largely stepped away from Hollywood to concentrate on her family and charitable work, particularly her longtime involvement with the Special Olympics.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: 'The Pitt' star Noah Wyle's 'Sexiest Man Alive' crown sparks backlash as fans fume: 'You've got to be kidding'
summary: Noah Wyle's People 'Sexiest Man Alive' crown divided fans, with critics naming Patrick Dempsey and Jonathan Bailey as better picks for the title.
story: After his Emmy win on Sunday, Wyle compared his "ER" triumph to his current success. The actor won Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series for his role in "The Pitt."
Noah Wyle has claimed the title of Hollywood's sexiest man — but some fans think People should have gone back to the drawing board.
The 55-year-old "The Pitt" star has been named People magazine's "Sexiest Man Alive" for 2026, sparking a social media debate over whether the longtime TV heartthrob was the right man for the title.
"Out of all of the people in the world…this is who you pick? You’ve got to be kidding," one critic fumed.
NOAH WYLE, MATT DAMON, LEONARDO DICAPRIO STILL CAPTIVATING AUDIENCES WELL INTO THEIR 50S
Noah Wyle's new title as People's 2026 "Sexiest Man Alive" has fans divided, with some celebrating the Hollywood veteran and others questioning the magazine's choice. (Jeff Lipsky/PEOPLE)
Another took a swipe at Wyle’s competition, writing, "Not even the sexiest in that show."
And one commenter wasn’t about to let the announcement slide without a pun.
"More like Noah WHY-le! Ha ha but no seriously who’d you actually pick?" the user joked, while another asked, "is this a joke?"
"Poor Noah. I like him. Good actor but he’s not sexiest man alive. Come on," another wrote.
"Not bad... not great..." one person assessed.
Noah Wyle appears on the cover of People magazine's "Sexiest Man Alive" issue. (Jeff Lipsky/PEOPLE)
The criticism came alongside plenty of support for Wyle, whose journey from "ER" favorite Dr. John Carter to leading man of "The Pitt" has brought him back into the spotlight.
Noah Wyle is turning heads — and raising eyebrows — after landing People's coveted "Sexiest Man Alive" crown at 55. (Jeff Lipsky/PEOPLE)
"Thank you for getting it right finally!" one fan declared.
"This is actually an incredible win for anyone who grew up watching ER. why did it take Hollywood this long to give him the crown," another wrote.
MATT DAMON SAYS HOLLYWOOD'S 'RUTHLESS' NATURE HAS TAKEN HIM AWAY FROM FATHERHOOD MORE THAN HE'D LIKE
One admirer argued that Wyle brings more to the table than a handsome face, writing, "#NoahWyle does not just have the looks. He's the whole damn package. That's why he's The Sexiest Man Alive!"
"Just accept we have a 55-year-old as the Sexiest Man Alive! Noah Wyle, just know that you’re hot!"
"I thought that sounded like a prank — just not in a million years did I think that this would be an honor bestowed on me," Noah Wyle told People of their decision. (Jeff Lipsky/PEOPLE)
Other social media users suggested alternative candidates.
"they could’ve just had patrick dempsey do it again if they wanted someone older," one commenter suggested.
Another backed a different contender, writing, "@Deancain would have been a good choice. Just saying."
And for fans still mourning last year's winner, one person offered a simple solution: "it’s not too late to choose jonathan bailey again."
Patrick Dempsey, Dean Cain and Jonathan Bailey were thrown out by some social media users as better options for the title. (Stefanie Keenan/WireImage; Paul Archuleta; Mauricio Santana)
For Wyle, the "Sexiest Man Alive" title marks another milestone in his Hollywood comeback.

The actor first became a household name as Dr. John Carter on "ER," spending years at the center of one of television's defining medical dramas before making his final appearance on the series in 2009.
Noah Wyle's career comeback on "The Pitt" has earned him critical acclaim. (Jeff Lipsky/PEOPLE)

Years later, he returned to the medical drama genre as Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch in "The Pitt," winning the Emmy for outstanding lead actor in a drama series in both 2025 and 2026 and introducing himself to a new generation of viewers.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Off-screen, the 55-year-old is a husband and father of three who has spoken candidly about the pressures of fame, his devotion to his family and his support for healthcare workers.
Wyle has three children — Owen and Auden from his first marriage to Tracy Warbin, and Frances with his wife, Sara Wells, whom he married in 2014.
Noah Wyle as Doctor John Carter in "ER." (Chris Haston/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
Wyle himself admitted the honor caught him off guard.

"I thought that sounded like a prank — just not in a million years did I think that this would be an honor bestowed on me," he told People editor-in-chief Charlotte Triggs in an exclusive cover interview.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
His wife, Sara, was more enthusiastic, encouraging him to embrace a title he initially struggled to believe was real.

"She was very pleased that this reflects well on her taste," Wyle said. "She thinks I’m a good guy and that the kind of person that I am and the kind of father I am, the kind of husband I am, is worth promoting. I thought, ‘Okay, if you say so.’"
His children also had some concerns.
Wyle told People magazine that his wife was "very pleased" with his new title. (Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for The Daily Front Row)
Wyle said his son immediately worried about the unwanted attention that could come with the new title.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"My son is super practical. He was like, ‘Oh, this is going to make my life so much harder now. But that’s cool, Dad. But also, you invite a lot of haters too.’ My older daughter was just like, ‘No way, no way.’ Because I think she’s going to tease me about this for the next 50 years."
While speaking with People, he credited fatherhood with changing his priorities and said becoming a parent helped prompt his decision to leave "ER."

title: Rob Riggle says Hollywood work is disappearing from LA: 'It's the exception now'
summary: Rob Riggle reveals why actors are fleeing Los Angeles as work dries up and shares his dream of moving back to his native Kansas City someday.
story: The "Christmas at the Kringles" actor told Fox News Digital he'd like to move back to the Midwest someday.
Rob Riggle said many people in the industry are leaving Los Angeles because the work has moved away.
The comedian, who stars in the upcoming holiday horror film "Christmas at the Kringles," told Fox News Digital that getting a job in the city is more the exception than the rule now.

"I think a lot has changed, the way things are done," he explained. "I used to be out here because I needed to be available to work here. A lot of the work isn't here anymore. I mean, a lot of it, the work is not here anymore. It's the exception now, if you get to work here. So that's one reason."
HOLLYWOOD STAR SOUNDS ALARM OVER DISAPPEARING JOBS AS PRODUCTIONS FLEE CALIFORNIA
Rob Riggle said that industry work is moving away from Los Angeles. (Variety via Getty Images)
Riggle said that actors don’t even need to be in L.A. to audition anymore.

"They don't even do that anymore. Like you don't get to go in anymore," he said. "You have to put yourself on tape standing in front of a white, opaque wall in your garage, trying to make a selfie video, reading with your neighbor, you know, or whoever's in the house, you know? It's terrible. It's just a terrible way to do business. And for whatever reason, that's what we get after COVID. So that's the new paradigm and it sucks."
WATCH HERE: ROB RIGGLE SAYS INDUSTRY WORK IS RARELY WORK IN LA
"I used to be out here because I needed to be available to work here. A lot of the work isn't here anymore."
The "Stepbrothers" actor added that "obviously there's economic reasons to move out."
The 56-year-old told Fox News Digital he would love to move back to his native Kansas City.
Rob Riggle stars in the new comedy-horror holiday film "Christmas at the Kringles." (Victoria Sirakova/Getty Images)
JANA KRAMER SAYS LOS ANGELES PRICED HER OUT OF THE CHILDHOOD SHE WANTED FOR HER KIDS

"I would love to make that happen," he admitted. "I don't know when that's going to happen. I've got some things here in California that need tending to, and maybe when I get to a place, once those things are tended to, I can make that move and, get back to, where — I've got a lot of family and friends back there. That was where I grew up and stuff. So it'd be nice if I could make it happen."
WATCH HERE: ROB RIGGLE ON WHY HE DECIDED TO DO HORROR-COMEDY ‘CHRISTMAS AT THE KRINGLES’
Riggle is promoting his new holiday horror-comedy "Christmas at the Kringles," which was actually shot in Los Angeles.
In the movie, Riggle plays a character named "Drunk Santa."
Rob Riggle said he plays a character called Drunk Santa. (Disney via Getty Images)

"So, I knew there was going to be a lot of fun right then just seeing that," he joked. "I was like, ‘Oh this is going to be fun. And then the story, the fact that we're mixing so many genres, comedy, horror, holiday — all kind of thrown into one thing and that I think makes it wildly entertaining all the way through. And then the cast and the director, the producers, like the whole team, I just thought, ‘My gosh, if nothing else, I'm going to have the best time ever, and that matters to me."
The cast also includes Ron Livingston, Rachel Bilson, Beverly D'Angelo and Donald Faison.
Riggle said his family has their Christmas locked down.
Rob Riggle sits with Ron Livingston while dressed as Santa in "Christmas at the Kringles." (19th Hole Productions)

"We don’t do chaos," he said after being asked about the holidays. "We are pretty good, I gotta say. We hunker down, you know, we get in early and we stay late and we do our shopping in advance. And I'm talking about food even. Like, we get that bunker thing going, so we don't have to go out if we don't want to."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
The former Marine noted that he’s spent past Christmases in some "unusual" places like Afghanistan.
Rob Riggle spent one Christmas in Afghanistan in 2001. (Getty Images)
CHRIS ROCK EXPOSES LA'S DARK ‘UNDERBELLY’ THAT PEOPLE PRETEND DOESN'T EXIST

"It was very early in that conflict," he said. "It was Christmas of 2001, and it was still a very dangerous place. And I remember looking out at the stars. It was a beautiful night. It was very cold, but it was clear, and you could see all the stars and it was very nice."

"The Hangover" actor said he "happened to be with some British special forces people that they're allowed to have a little rum ration. We are not. And so, they were gracious enough to give us a little holiday spirit, which was nice. And so we all celebrated together, and it was a unique moment."
'ANT-MAN' STAR EVANGELINE LILLY SAYS SHE LEFT HOLLYWOOD BECAUSE SHE 'ALWAYS HATED BEING FAMOUS'
The Marines, he said, taught him how to be a leader.

"Perseverance, I think, is the key," he said. "Discipline and consistency, discipline, perseverance, those simple things. Just those two things really, perseverance and discipline and you'll win. If you just stay at it you'll accomplish what you set out to accomplish, but it's going to take those two things and those two things aren't easy. That's the trick. Those two things are not easy, but if you do them you'll get the results."
"Christmas at the Kringles" opens in theaters on Oct. 30.

title: Meghan Markle's acting comeback suffers major blow as Netflix 'safety net' disappears: expert
summary: Meghan Markle is no longer in talks to join "The Gentlemen" as sources allege Netflix leaked casting news to boost the show's publicity online.
story: Doug Eldridge, founder of Achilles PR, explains why Meghan Markle may need to break from her public image and take on unexpected acting roles to revive her acting career.
Meghan Markle is no longer in talks to join "The Gentlemen," with friends alleging she was "used to help promote" the Netflix series.

Royal experts told Fox News Digital that the Duchess of Sussex's "safety net" with Netflix "is gone" as uncertainty surrounding her relationship with the streaming service threatens to derail her acting comeback before it even gets off the ground.

"Harry and Meghan's champion inside Netflix, Bela Bajaria, has recently left the streaming service," British broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "The previous safety net is gone. Unfortunately for Meghan, she may want to jump straight into a top acting role, but there is far more stacked against it happening."
MEGHAN MARKLE’S ACTING RETURN COULD SPARK FRESH PROBLEMS WITH PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON: EXPERT

Meghan, Duchess of Sussex speaks onstage during the 2025 TIME100 Summit at Jazz at Lincoln Center on April 23, 2025, in New York City. Sources close to the duchess told The Telegraph she is no longer in talks to join "The Gentlemen" on Netflix. (2025 Getty Images)
Variety reported Bajaria was leaving Netflix after nearly 10 years with the company. According to the outlet, around 1,000 employees were laid off.
Bajaria was leaving Netflix after nearly 10 years with the company.
"What I find most revealing is that Meghan's camp now appears comfortable publicly criticizing Netflix," Kinsey Schofield, host of "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital.
Bela Bajaria, then-chief content officer at Netflix, attends the 31st annual Screen Actors Guild Awards at Shrine Auditorium and Expo Hall in Los Angeles, on Feb. 23, 2025. (Getty Images)

"This was one of their most important commercial partners. You don't typically throw a company under the bus when you're counting on them to finance your next big project. To me, this is the clearest indication yet that their relationship with Netflix has effectively come to an end."
WATCH: MEGHAN MARKLE NEEDS A HOLLYWOOD REINVENTION, PR EXPERT SAYS

The Duchess of Sussex was reportedly under consideration for a role in the third season of Guy Ritchie's Netflix drama following her move back to the U.K. with Prince Harry. However, sources close to Meghan have accused Netflix of leaking news of her potential involvement to boost publicity for the show.
"Some people in her camp feel she was used to help promote Season 2, because they knew it wasn't as good as the first season and had already commissioned a third," one source told The Telegraph.
Theo James attends "The Gentlemen" U.K. series global premiere at the Theatre Royal in London on March 5, 2024. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

"It's the oldest marketing trick in the book: get a big name to read a script, then leak that you're 'in conversation' with them when, in reality, nothing is particularly far along. The whole thing left a bit of a sour taste in the Sussex camp's mouth. Needless to say, Netflix got what it wanted: huge viewing figures for Season 2 and a lot of publicity."
Meghan Markle’s return to acting comes after a series of post-royal ventures, including her Netflix lifestyle series, "With Love, Meghan." (Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell and Netflix for comment.
Schofield told Fox News Digital she wouldn't be surprised if Meghan's relationship with Netflix had soured.
Meghan Markle's As Ever spread is seen here. (As Ever)

"Netflix has already withdrawn from its investment in As Ever," Schofield said. "Meghan herself credited Bajaria with recognizing the television potential in her homemade gifts. She told the TIME100 Summit that 'With Love, Meghan,' her lifestyle show, was Bajaria's idea."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Meghan Markle is reportedly eyeing a return to acting after years spent building a new identity outside the royal family. (Tommaso Boddi/Getty Images)

"Now, after Bajaria's departure, we're hearing accusations that Netflix exploited Meghan for publicity," Schofield said. "Does that sound like a relationship with a promising future? I suspect Meghan's camp feels comfortable criticizing Netflix because there's nothing left to protect."
A source close to Netflix has pushed back on the accusations, telling The Times, "This is not a show in need of stunt casting."
Guy Ritchie attends "The Gentlemen" Season 2 world premiere at Guildhall on Sept. 2, 2026, in London, England. (Getty Images)
A Netflix consultant who worked closely with Bajaria told The Times that Meghan and Harry's relationship with the streaming service has been called into question.
Meghan Markle was previously the host of a lifestyle series on Netflix titled "With Love, Meghan." (Jake Rosenberg/Netflix © 2025)

"Effectively, their biggest champion has gone, and they are uncertain about who will be shouting for their cause in the future," the source said. "Teams at the company were well aware of how she was fiercely loyal to the couple and determined to prove they were a successful signing, even when the response from viewers was different."

"The Gentlemen," which is set in the U.K., was renewed for a third season in August. Deadline previously reported that talks about Meghan joining the cast were in the "very early stages," while The Hollywood Reporter reported that the role "is currently being written, so it's unclear how many episodes she would appear in."
Meghan Markle on the red carpet for "Suits," circa 2015. (Mike Coppola/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital that Meghan "did nothing to thwart all the speculation" sooner, noting that Netflix also did not issue a statement to address the casting rumors.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's Hollywood dreams are in jeopardy as they face a brand crisis over collapsed deals and fading public interest, according to royal experts. (Aaron Chown/PA Images)
"They benefited from the additional coverage even if, as they claim, it wasn't needed," Fordwich said. "Such a high-profile show would have been a high-profile win for Meghan."

In March 2026, Netflix and Meghan announced the end of their partnership involving her lifestyle brand, As Ever, with the Duchess of Sussex moving forward independently. As Ever launched in 2025, about a month after the premiere of "With Love, Meghan." The show released two seasons and a holiday special in 2025. Reports in January 2026 indicated that it would not return for a third season.
Meghan Markle, a former American actress, became the Duchess of Sussex when she married Prince Harry, a British prince, in 2018. (Ben Stansall-WPA Pool/Getty Images)

Harry and Meghan first partnered with Netflix in 2020 under a deal reportedly worth $100 million. Their projects included the 2022 series "Harry & Meghan" and "Live to Lead," 2023's "Heart of Invictus" and 2024's "Polo." Although reports in July 2025 suggested the original agreement would not be renewed, Netflix announced a new multiyear, first-look deal with Archewell Productions in August 2025.

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, Nicole Avant, and Ted Sarandos attend Netflix's "BEEF" Season 2 Montecito Tastemaker at a private residence on April 10, 2026, in Montecito, California. (Stefanie Keenan)

According to The Times, Netflix previously scrapped an animated project from the couple, while little has been reported about their planned film adaptations of the war memoir "No Way Out" and the romance novels "Meet Me at the Lake" and "The Wedding Date."

It is unclear whether Netflix will pick up a potential documentary about Harry's late mother, Princess Diana, ahead of the 30th anniversary of her death in 2027. People magazine reported that Harry is exploring projects, but no documentary has been finalized or confirmed.

Diana, Princess of Wales, wearing a cream lace gown with a scalloped neckline designed by Murray Arbeid and the Lover's Knot diamond and pearl tiara, smiles as she attends a dinner at the British Ambassador's Residence in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 11, 1985. (Getty Images)

"'The Gentlemen' is an established Guy Ritchie production with its own audience," Schofield said. "The suggestion that Netflix needed Meghan to rescue its viewing figures is quite a claim from someone whose own lifestyle series struggled to become a mainstream hit."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle returned to the U.K. six years after leaving for California. (Getty Images)
"Meghan's royal connections might get her into the room, but they don't guarantee her a successful acting career. At some point, the work has to speak for itself."

Before marrying Harry in 2018, Meghan played Rachel Zane in "Suits" for seven seasons. In 2022, Meghan told Variety that she was "done" with acting. She has since filmed a cameo in the upcoming film "Close Personal Friends," which stars Lily Collins and Jack Quaid.

Alysa Nahmias and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, attend a special screening of Roadside Attractions' "Cookie Queens" at AMC The Grove 14 in Los Angeles on July 28, 2026. (Roadside Attractions via Getty Images)

Sources told People magazine that Meghan and Harry have been discussing her return to acting "for some time." The outlet reported that Meghan is "excited" about returning to the profession and is exploring opportunities.
Meghan Markle attends the Womenswear Spring-Summer 2026 show during Paris Fashion Week on Oct. 5, 2025, in Paris, France. (Andrea Cremascoli/Getty Images)

"Meghan Markle has repeatedly told us she was finished with acting," Schofield said. "During her 2017 engagement interview, she said she'd 'ticked this box.' Now, after six years in Hollywood and several attempts to reinvent herself, she's now reportedly entertaining a return to the profession she so confidently walked away from. Sure, a role in an established Guy Ritchie production would have given her an opportunity to change the conversation about her professional accomplishments. But I also think the timing of the story is revealing."
Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, attends the Balenciaga Womenswear Spring/Summer 2026 show during Paris Fashion Week on Oct. 4, 2025, in Paris, France. (Getty Images for Balenciaga)

"Harry and Meghan had just returned to Britain, a move that could easily be interpreted as an acknowledgment that their Hollywood ambitions hadn't worked out," Schofield said. "Suddenly, we're hearing about Meghan's potential acting comeback. The Sussexes seem determined to turn every bit of publicity into a much larger PR strategy. The problem is that their PR ambitions continue to outpace their professional accomplishments."
Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner believes Meghan's desire to return to acting, whether in Hollywood or the U.K., is genuine.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Actress Meghan Markle visits AOL Studios in New York City on March 17, 2016. (FilmMagic/Getty Images)

"The role which brought her to fame in ‘Suits’ proves she is an actress of quality," he said. "If she wanted to return to acting, which I believe is still a passion, then she could bring great credit to any production."
Bajaria's departure amid layoffs at Netflix raises further questions about the future of Harry and Meghan's projects with the streaming service.
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, participates in a Scar Tree Walk in Melbourne, Australia, on April 16, 2026, during a four-day visit with the Duke of Sussex. (Asanka Ratnayake/Getty Images)

"I suspect Harry and Meghan recognized that their Hollywood experiment wasn't delivering the success they expected," Schofield said. "Their return to Britain gives them something Los Angeles can't offer — proximity to the monarchy."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Brooke Hogan blasts ‘fake, greedy people’ after Hulk’s Florida home sale: ‘Enjoy your dirty money’
summary: Brooke Hogan accused unnamed friends and family of exploiting Hulk Hogan for profit after his Clearwater Beach mansion sold for $5.9 million.
story: HGTV "Rock the Block" contestant Brooke Hogan details the emotional fallout of her relationship with her late dad, Hulk Hogan, sharing how his absence still shapes her drive.
Brooke Hogan is lashing out at the "fake, greedy people" she claims profited from her late father Hulk Hogan as she mourns the sale of the wrestling legend's Florida home.

Last week, Hulk's 5,400-square-foot, beachfront mansion in Clearwater Beach sold for $5.9 million after it was originally listed for nearly $11 million in January, according to TMZ. The outlet also reported that the neighboring guest cottage sold separately for $2.8 million.
Hulk, who was born Terry Bollea, died at age 71 in July 2025 after suffering cardiac arrest at his home in Clearwater Beach. The WWE icon's cause of death was later determined to be a heart attack.
NICK HOGAN HELPS GUIDE HULKAMANIA INTO FUTURE WITH SPORTS BAR OUTSIDE MSG, SHARES THOUGHTS ON FATHER'S LEGACY

In a series of emotional posts shared to her Instagram Stories Monday, Brooke reflected on losing the home where she shared memories with her father while accusing unnamed friends and family members of exploiting him for their own gain.
The 38-year-old TV personality also took aim at what she described as "dirty money," claiming some people only appeared "at the end" of her father's life "to collect."
"The sick feeling is indescribable," Brooke wrote in one post alongside a photo of the house with a red and white SOLD sticker at the top.
Brooke Hogan slammed "fake, greedy people" after the sale of her late father Hulk Hogan's home.  (K Mazur/WireImage)
"This house was where dad and Jen envisioned growing old together," she added, referring to Hulk's ex-wife Jennifer McDaniel, to whom he was married from 2010 to 2021.
NETFLIX DOCUMENTARY DIRECTOR ON HULK HOGAN'S TRUMP SUPPORT AND THE BACKLASH THAT FOLLOWED HIM TO THE END
"Where we brought him back to…surgery after surgery," Brooke continued. "Pool days. The smell of gasoline in his garage. His workouts downstairs."

"We cooked, we watched Jerry springer, we played music, we cried," she recalled. "I walked in that garage every visit and hugged him right when he’d open the garage door. I’d sit next to him for hours in the chair he died in."
Hulk's 5,400-square-foot, beachfront mansion in Clearwater Beach, Florida sold for $5.9 million after it was originally listed for nearly $11 million in January. (AFP via Getty Images)
KRISTIN CAVALLARI SAYS SHE LEARNED A PAINFUL $250K LESSON INVOLVING HER FATHER AT 22
"His whole environment, his energy, his work, his relationships: First Jen — who no one but me treated with respect. Then I was gone…the truth teller… I’m sure to everyone’s delight."
"And now it’s all gone. Sold for profit. Just like him…used for f-----g everyone else’s gain. Saddest ending I’ve ever seen. You know who TF you are," Brooke concluded.
KRISTIN CAVALLARI CUT FATHER OUT OF HER LIFE AFTER HE CROSSED ‘MAJOR LINE’ INVOLVING HER KIDS
Hogan shared her emotional reaction to the sale in several Instagram posts. (Brooke Hogan/Instagram)

In another post, Brooke uploaded an image in which she was seen posing with Hulk a dock outside the house, writing, "Let’s not forget who was there for the 15 years before the vultures swooped in conveniently."

Brooke went on to share a series of photos documenting the years that she spent by her father's side, writing that she "adored," loved and "cherished" him. She also posted images of pill bottles that were labeled with Hulk's name, noting that she "tracked every med."
CRYSTAL HEFNER FELT 'ABSOLUTELY BRAINWASHED' DURING HUGH HEFNER MARRIAGE, REVEALS STRICT PLAYBOY MANSION RULES
The "Brooke Knows Best" star also recalled how she and McDaniel helped care for Hulk during his health struggles.
Brooke blasted "vultures" who she said profited from Hulk. (Brooke Hogan Instagram )
"Jen and I were the nurse crew. Notebooks, records, prescription pickups, overnights, switching shifts," Brooke wrote.
"This woman spent more time in the trenches than ANY of us did," she continued. "He LOVED her dearly. And she loved him."
"She wanted to be there till his last breath despite the trauma she endured that I witnessed..," Brooke added.
OZZY AND SHARON OSBOURNE'S LONGTIME LOS ANGELES HOME HITS THE MARKET FOR $17M AFTER HIS DEATH AT 76
Brooke claimed that McDaniel "asked for nothing" following her split from Hulk. She wrote that McDaniel could have "fought for money" but instead "vanished" without launching a "smear campaign."
Describing McDaniel as "hilarious," Brooke recalled the two having "girl days" together. She praised her former stepmother as "pure love and grace."
"Their breakup was devastating for me," Brooke wrote. "I loved her, but I knew my dad was in the best care with her too."
"DEVOTION was an UNDERSTATEMENT," she added.
Brooke heaped praise on Hulk's ex-wife Jennifer McDaniel. (WireImage)
Alongside photos of Hogan recovering from surgeries, Brooke recalled how she and McDaniel repeatedly accompanied him to the hospital.
"We did surgery… after surgery… after surgery," she wrote.

In one photo, Brooke pointed out blood on McDaniel's shirt and missing fingernails. She posted images of Hulk standing in the hospital room, writing, "I'm taking the photo. You see anyone else there? Whole room… no one else?"

Brooke then shared a photo that was taken during a July 2025 episode of "WWE SmackDown!" following Hulk's death. In the photo, WWE stars, several wrestling legends and production crew were seen gathered onstage for the traditional 10-bell salute in memory of Hulk.
Brooke also shared a photo that was taken during WWE's tribute to Hulk on "Smackdown!" (Brooke Hogan Instagram)
"Not ONE of these people stayed longer than an hour in the hospital… if they even showed," Brooke wrote.

"And I’ve had to hear everyone say I’m the jerk for stepping away from the toxic behavior and brainwashing, fake, greedy people… ‘I should have been there.’ ‘Everyone else’ was there till the end. NO. They were there AT the end. To collect," she wrote on a photo of herself with Hulk.
Brooke shared another image of the Hulk's home, writing, "Enjoy your dirty money. You took my dad."
However, Brooke later pushed back against reports that interpreted her posts as an attack on WWE stars, insisting that was not her intention.
DISGUSTING TROLLS ATTACK HULK HOGAN'S DAUGHTER FOR STARTING EMOTIONAL POST ABOUT DAD WITH A BIKINI PICTURE
Brooke recalled memories from spending time with Hulk at his Florida home. (Brooke Hogan Instagram )
"Hey reporters: I don't have beef with the stars of WWE. Nor did I say that. Do your job right or don't do it at all," she wrote in a follow-up post on her Instagram Story.
Brooke explained that she was criticizing people who she said "show up to public tributes" despite not supporting her father privately when she was "in the trenches with him."
"But they'll show up to get their face on camera," she wrote, adding, "That includes so called ‘friends' AND family."

In another post, Brooke elaborated on her accusations as she blasted unnamed people who she claimed "only visited him if he payed [sic] for it" and others who "got a paycheck if they pretended they were his friend."
She also called out "the 'yes men' who were too afraid to protect him with truth" and "the ones who promised me they'd do the right thing when he died."

"Apparently EVERYONE will show up at the end if you're famous enough and they can profit off your demise," Brooke concluded.
The two, who were once extremely close, were estranged at the time of Hulk's death.  (Brooke Hogan Instagram )

Brooke and Hulk were once extremely close and their father-daughter relationship was a major part of their reality series "Hogan Knows Best," which ran from 2005 to 2007. However, their relationship became complicated over the years and Brooke was estranged from Hulk during the final two years of his life.

In July 2023, Hulk amended his will to exclude Brooke and her descendants, leaving her brother Nick as the sole beneficiary of his probate estate. The "Rocky III" star shared Brooke and Nick, 36, with his ex-wife Linda Hogan. Hulk was married to Sky Daily from 2023 until his death.

Brooke said her posts were directed at unnamed friends and family.  (Brooke Hogan Instagram )

Brooke has maintained that her estrangement from Hulk was not due to a single falling-out. After Hulk died, Brooke said she ultimately stepped away following a series of "respectful disagreements" with her father that took an emotional toll on her.

Hulk never publicly addressed his estrangement from Brooke or his decision to formally remove her from his will. However, a source told Us Weekly in March 2025 that the wrestling icon had told people he did not know why his daughter had stopped speaking to him. title: Jon Gosselin claims he's 'perfect strangers now' with six of his kids after years of no contact
summary: Jon Gosselin reveals he hasn't spoken to six of his eight children in years, calling them "perfect strangers" amid Collin Gosselin's memoir.
story: ‘In the Shadow of Eight’ author tells Fox News Digital about his alleged childhood abuse and isolation.
Jon Gosselin hasn't spoken with most of his children in more than a decade.

The reality star, who appeared on "Jon & Kate Plus 8" before his divorce from ex-wife Kate Gosselin, admitted that his strained relationships with six of his kids have made them "perfect strangers now."

Jon Gosselin admitted he hasn't spoken to most of his children in more than one decade. (Tommaso Boddi)

Jon and Kate – who have twins Mady and Cara and sextuplets Hannah, Leah, Alexis, Joel, Aaden and Collin — announced their divorce in a broadcast episode of the show.
Collin and Hannah began living with Jon in 2018, when Jon admitted that while Collin went "no contact" with his siblings, Hannah was still speaking with her mother.
'JON & KATE' STAR COLLIN GOSSELIN CLAIMS MOTHER ZIP-TIED AND LOCKED HIM IN BASEMENT ROOM AS A CHILD

HAYDEN PANETTIERE AND THE CHILD STARS WHOSE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR MOMAGERS TURNED COMPLICATED

title: Natalie Portman says being sexualized as a child star forced her to become a 'good girl' as protection
summary: Natalie Portman reveals how she built a "good girl" persona to counter childhood sexualization in Hollywood and why it became a lasting trap.
story: James Sexton, Esq., explains how emotional withdrawal develops between couples, and why renewed attention, affection and mindfulness can reveal whether both partners remain invested.
Natalie Portman learned early that growing up in Hollywood meant protecting herself from the very image that made her famous.

The Oscar-winning actress opened up about the lasting impact of being sexualized as a child star, revealing how she carefully crafted a "good girl" image to shield herself from unwanted attention – only to find that the persona followed her well into adulthood.
Portman began her career in films featuring dark themes, such as 1994 thriller "Léon: The Professional," "Heat" and "Beautiful Girls."
BELLA THORNE SAYS HOLLYWOOD TREATED HER LIKE A KID ON SCREEN AND AN ADULT OFF CAMERA
Natalie Portman said she adopted a "good girl" persona as a child star to protect herself from being sexualized in Hollywood. (Patrick Camboulive/Sygma)

As Portman navigated the pressures of Hollywood at a young age, she and her parents made a deliberate effort to separate her on-screen persona from who she was in real life. Rather than embrace the provocative image associated with some of her early roles, Portman maintained a more reserved public image. She chose conservative, age-appropriate clothing for red carpet appearances while remaining focused on her education and academic success.

"I think there was a conscious effort, because I was depicted as this sexualized Lolita, that I wanted to be like, ‘No, I’m serious, I’m a good girl, I’m a prude, I’m smart, I’m a student,’ emphasizing that as almost a safety mechanism," she told Harper's Bazaar.

As her career progressed, Portman continued to gravitate toward complex, emotionally demanding roles. She eventually earned an Oscar for her performance in "Black Swan" and another nomination for "Jackie."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Natalie Portman won an Oscar for her performance in "Black Swan." (James Devaney/WireImage)

But as her career flourished, Portman found that the serious image she had carefully cultivated, coupled with the demanding roles she continued to play, created a lasting misconception about her personality.

"But then, over time, it became like everyone thinks I’m really serious," Portman noted. "I’m very silly, and I love to laugh more than anything, and I love to goof off. People always think I’m a perfectionist, I think, because of 'Black Swan.' I’m the opposite. I’m forgiving with myself. In college, we had a phrase: ‘Done, not good.’"
After spending much of her career exploring darker, more complex characters, Portman said her priorities have shifted toward bringing audiences a sense of happiness.
Natalie Portman said she's focusing on bringing more joy to audiences after years of portraying darker, emotionally complex characters. (Dominique Charriau/WireImage)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Right now, it’s a lot of joy," she told the outlet of the current phase of her career. "I think it’s both for myself and what I hope to offer an audience, because it just feels … I mean, every time has dark moments, but it feels like there’s a lot of really heavy stuff going on. It’s just ever-present in our face, and so it does feel like the biggest service you can do right now as an artist is to deliver some joy."

Portman has also found joy in her personal life, recently welcoming a child with her partner, Tanguy Destable. A few weeks after welcoming her third child, Portman told Harper's Bazaar she's been "full of wonder and joy at this magical little human."
