title: Kevin Bleyer, an Emmy-winning ‘Daily Show’ writer, killed in car crash at 54
summary: Kevin Bleyer, a “The Daily Show” writer, died in a car crash Sunday, his wife said in an Instagram statement.
story: Kevin Bleyer, a “The Daily Show” writer, died in a car crash Sunday, his wife said in an Instagram statement.
He was 54.
“I am devastated, heartbroken, shattered,” Nella Vera wrote. “My heart has a hole in it that will never be filled,” she  posted alongside a picture of him.
Bleyer’s family said the accident happened on a rural road in Millrift, Pennsylvania, Variety reported. He had a home in the area.
Bleyer worked on “The Daily Show” with Jon Stewart for nine years and an additional eight years as a writer for “Politically Incorrect” with Bill Maher and Dennis Miller.
He won four Primetime Emmy Awards, a Writers Guild Award and a Peabody Award for his work.
Bleyer wrote speeches for then-President Barack Obama and then-New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio, among others. He also authored books and plays.

title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17 billion, creating delivery giant
summary: Delivery giant DoorDash is buying to-your-door grocery service Instacart for $17 billion, the company announced Thursday.
story: Delivery giant DoorDash is buying to-your-door grocery service Instacart for $17 billion, the company announced Thursday.
The deal means users will be able to order groceries and items from other retailers via DoorDash and its delivery network.

The companies said Instacart customers can now shop at more than 50,000 additional stores on top of the nearly 100,000 stores on the Instacart platform today. DashPass and Instacart+ members will now also pay one membership fee instead of two.
DoorDash is expected to keep the Instacart brand and its technology. Until the transaction closes, DoorDash and Instacart will continue to operate as separate and independent companies.

“Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” Instacart CEO  Chris Rogers said.
DoorDash shares gained more than 9% in pre-market trading Thursday.
The deal represents the latest chapter of consolidation in the delivery industry. Last year, DoorDash bought United Kingdom-based Deliveroo, while Uber now owns Postmates ​and Delivery Hero.
DoorDash has emerged as the most successful stand-alone online delivery platform in America, commanding some two-thirds of all food delivery volumes as of 2024, according to Bloomberg data.
But over the past year, the company has seen its share price decline by approximately a third, largely due to rising costs.
Instacart, meanwhile,  reached the pinnacle of its success during the Covid pandemic, when lockdowns sent millions of consumers to their phones to order grocery deliveries.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

But the company’s stock has gone nowhere over the past two years, as Instacart struggled to find new paths to growth while facing increasing competition from Amazon and Walmart’s grocery delivery offerings.

While a merger would create cost savings by allowing the combined company to reduce its corporate workforce and split some expenses, it’s not clear how much more money there remains that can be squeezed out of delivery customers.
Americans who eat at home have begun to complain about the price of food delivery — and the pinch has only worsened this year amid soaring fuel costs, which have led to new fees and surcharges.
A recent debate about the cost of having a burrito delivered went viral, as social media users argued over whether $20 was a reasonable price to pay to have the Tex-Mex treat delivered.

Platforms such as DoorDash and Instacart have also faced legal scrutiny over how they treat those who make deliveries for their respective platforms. Last month, DoorDash settled with New York City regulators for $131.5 million to resolve charges it deprived workers of millions of dollars in tips.

“Simply put, we screwed up,” the San ‌Francisco-based ⁠company said in a statement. “Our mistakes meant some Dashers were underpaid or paid late. While these mistakes weren’t intentional, that doesn’t make them okay.”
The proposed transaction was first reported by tech website The Information and The Wall Street Journal.

title: Protests erupt in Spain after train crash kills dozens
summary: Protests erupted in Madrid as Spain began mourning the 68 people killed and dozens injured in the country’s deadliest train crash in decades.
story: URDA, Spain — Spain began three days of mourning Thursday after at least 69 people were killed and dozens more injured in the country’s deadliest train crash in decades. But anger is mounting about the alleged incompetence that allowed the accident to happen and protesters clashed with police overnight outside the country’s transport ministry.
Once considered one of the country’s crowning achievements, Spain’s high-speed rail network had not endured a deadly crash since it came into service over 30 years ago.
After the second train accident in less than a year, the tragedy has deepened the feeling among many that there is something broken in Spanish society.  The crash follows weeks of protests.

Rising costs and a housing shortage that is pricing many Spaniards out of the housing market, have already triggered massive and sometimes deadly protests across the country, and piled the pressure on the Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

On Wednesday, four weeks before the country goes to the polls in a national election, Sanchez visited the site in the central province of Toledo where a quiet stretch of rail lined by olive groves had been turned into a scene of devastation.

Pictures showed several carriages lying on their sides next to the tracks and others twisted at angles, their wheels sheared off. Debris was strewn around the scene of the accident in the countryside in the province of Toledo after one train crashed into another that was stationary on the line.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Hundreds of emergency workers, firefighters, police and soldiers attended the scene to rescue survivors and recover bodies, before cranes were brought in to move parts of the damaged trains late Wednesday.

title: Their record is strong. Their roster is battered. Can the Thunder still contend for an NBA title?
summary: Oklahoma City lost two key players — Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace — in the first month of the season to injuries.
story: The Oklahoma City Thunder’s win on opening night of the new NBA season was a reminder of everything that makes the league’s 2025 champion a prime contender to win again.
Barely one week later, those aspirations have already been damaged.

Thunder star Jalen Williams, the team’s second-leading scorer and best all-around defender during its title run two seasons ago, fractured a fibula and dislocated his left ankle in a gruesome injury Sunday. The same night, Cason Wallace, a hounding defender and accurate shooter in his own right, tore the labrum in his shoulder.

Thunder general manager Sam Presti didn’t specify how long both will miss, but they are expected to miss months, at a minimum, putting their availability for any playoff run — especially a deep one — in serious doubt. Jeff Stotts, an athletic trainer who runs a site that tracks sports injuries, wrote that since 2005, just one player had sustained a torn labrum like Wallace’s and returned later that season.

“We’ll get them back, we’ll get them healthy, but we got a lot of basketball to play in front of us,” Presti said Monday. “We got to put it together, figure out what the next steps are, because this is part of the business that we’re in.”

Getting Williams back healthy had been central to Oklahoma City’s goal of returning to the NBA Finals. Injuries sidelined Williams for more than half of last season, and he also missed time during last season’s Western Conference finals, which the Thunder lost in seven games to San Antonio.

When San Antonio and Oklahoma City met on opening night, with Oklahoma City winning on the road, it was widely seen as a preview of the spring, when the two teams with loaded rosters featuring superstars still in their 20s were expected again to face off for the right to make the Finals.

“It’s obviously going to be tough without a player” like Williams, Thunder guard and two-time league MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said. “But he’s not gone forever. He’ll be back better than ever, and we know it. We’ve just got to hold the fort down until he comes back.”

The Thunder aren’t the only team whose season has already been upended by injuries. Minnesota Timberwolves All-Star guard Anthony Edwards is expected to miss around two months after his right knee required an arthroscopic procedure, ESPN reported. A right knee injury will also sideline Utah Jazz star forward Jaren Jackson Jr. for a reported six to eight weeks, while an ankle injury will sideline Orlando Magic star Paolo Banchero at least a month. Indiana Pacers All-Star Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) and Orlando guard Jalen Suggs (right knee) also will miss time.

Drawing a connection between some of the acute injuries, like Williams’ freak fracture, and cumulative injuries such as the knee that has bothered Edwards for months is difficult, said Dr. Tarek Souryal, a former president of the NBA Physicians Association who was the Dallas Mavericks’ team doctor for more than two decades.

“What you’re witnessing is most likely a statistical aberration, not necessarily evidence of a systemic problem,” Souryal said. “A cluster of injuries, however unusual or alarming, does not by itself establish a causal relationship.”

Wallace and Williams are homegrown talents, drafted and developed by Oklahoma City into centerpieces of the 2025 championship team. The Thunder, under Presti, drafted and traded so well that their depth was often unparalleled around the NBA, with capable emerging contributors backing up more established starters.

The current collective bargaining agreement between the league and the players union, however, makes it financially difficult for a team to keep together a core of players for longer than a few seasons once they get old enough, and perform well enough, to command lucrative long-term extensions.

title: Can a $500 Keurig earn its counter space?
summary: The plastic-free Keurig Alta Coffee and Espresso Maker recently launched and we put it to the test for three weeks to see if it was actually worth the upgrade. Here’s who it’s best for and whether it’s worth the $499 price tag.
story: My family is full Keurig power users. We’ve had them in every family kitchen that I’ve ever walked into. We practically used K-cups as decor.

Coffee makers are changing, though. Lavazza’s Tabli brews compressed coffee tabs without a capsule. Caraway’s new drip coffee maker has a stainless steel and glass brew path. Now, Keurig has the Alta, a $499.99 coffee and espresso maker built for its new plastic-free AltaRounds. It still takes K-cups.

We received the Alta before launch and spent three weeks testing it alongside other coffee makers. I concentrated on the espresso drinks because those are what I spend money on when I’m out. My most recent large iced latte, with regular milk and three shots of espresso, cost $9.53. At that price, I did a little arithmetic.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
What is the Keurig Alta Single Serve Coffee and Espresso Maker
Keurig Alta Single Serve Coffee and Espresso Maker

The Keurig Alta is a single-serve coffee and espresso maker with a built-in milk frother. It brews AltaRounds, portions of ground coffee (think: small chocolate bonbon) pressed into a round and covered with a plant-based coating in place of a plastic or aluminum capsule. When we spoke with the Keurig team, they said the plant-based ingredient was seaweed. It also accepts regular K-Cup pods.

The machine reads a code on each round to set the brewing style, pressure and temperature. Its touchscreen has drink recipes, and the frother can prepare hot or cold milk foam. It can connect to Wi-Fi, allowing new drink recipes to be automatically added during system updates. You can also texture the milk manually.
How I tested it

We tested the Alta over three weeks, including comparisons with other machines in our office. I spent most of my time on the espresso drinks. I wanted to see how those drinks tasted, how much counter space the machine needed and whether the cost made sense against my coffee shop purchases.

We measured its footprint against the Lavazza Tablì and Caraway coffee makers, compared its milk-frothing noise with our office Keurig and checked what happened when used rounds sat in the waste bin for several days.
My experience with the Keurig Alta
I liked the Alta’s looks and the flexibility of having coffee, espresso and a milk frother in one machine.
It looks good on the counter

The matte white finish is sleek, and the machine is about 11 inches wide. That feels reasonable for a brewer with a milk frother beside it. I liked how the two fit together without needing room for a separate appliance.
You can keep using your K-cups

The Alta accepts both AltaRounds and regular K-Cups. That makes the switch easier if you already have a favorite coffee or a cabinet full of pods. You can try the rounds and still brew the coffee you already own. We still recommend using a reusable K-cup versus the disposable ones, due to the environmental impact of the traditional K-cups.
It also gives the Alta some flexibility while Keurig adds more coffees to the new format. For my family, compatibility with the existing stash is a selling point.
The waste bin has a useful drain

With some other plastic-free pods our testers have tried, we’ve seen visible mold develop quickly when we didn’t empty the waste container every day. We left several used AltaRounds in the Alta’s bin for several days and didn’t see the same thing.
The bin has two levels, with used rounds above and water draining below. Keeping the two apart may have helped.
The flavor is still very Keurig
To our testers, the coffee tasted much like standard Keurig coffee, perhaps with a small improvement in flavor. If you already enjoy Keurig, that may suit you perfectly.
I wouldn’t spend $500 expecting a dramatic improvement in taste alone. I’d want to use the espresso options and frother regularly enough to justify the upgrade.
It takes up a lot of counter depth
The Alta measured about 15 inches deep without its water tank and 19 inches with it. The second number is the one to plan around.

For comparison, our Lavazza Tablì measured about 12 inches without its tank and 15 inches with it. The Caraway coffee maker was about 11.5 inches deep. The Alta’s roughly 11-inch width is manageable, but it reaches much farther back on the counter than those machines.

I’d consider appliance rollers or a sliding tray underneath so I could turn or pull it forward to reach the water tank. If you’re short on counter space, measure the spot and leave room to get at the tank before committing.
Frothing peaked at 75 decibels
During our latte comparison, the Alta peaked at about 75 decibels while frothing milk. Our office Keurig peaked at 70 decibels during frothing.
The rounds still come with wrappers

AltaRounds have no plastic or aluminum capsule, but each one comes in a foil-based freshness wrapper, according to Keurig. You’ll still have packaging to deal with even if you compost the used coffee. However, Keurig’s press release states that “The company is validating a paper-based wrapper and is committed to transitioning to a recyclable paper-based wrap in 2027.”
Is it worth it?

At $499.99, I think the Alta makes the most sense for someone who already likes Keurig coffee, wants to make espresso drinks with a built-in frother and will use it to replace regular coffee shop purchases. I’d have a harder time justifying the price for someone who mainly wants a better-tasting cup of basic Keurig coffee.

My $9.53 coffee shop order was a large iced latte with regular milk and an extra shot, for three shots total. For an Alta version, I used Keurig’s announced prices for one Single Shot round and one Double Shot round. That means using two rounds for each latte. This estimate assumes both are available and can be selected for the four-box starter offer.

Keurig has priced an eight-count box of Single Shot rounds at $9.99 and Double Shot rounds at $10.99. That puts the coffee for a three-shot drink at about $2.62. With the $1.50-per-box subscription discount, it falls to about $2.25.

Milk costs extra. For this estimate, I allowed eight fluid ounces of dairy milk at an assumed $5 per half gallon, which adds about 63 cents. That brings the ingredients to about $3.25 per latte, or $2.87 with a subscription.
I used Keurig’s single- and double-shot labels for the comparison. The café’s espresso dose and milk quantity could differ.

The machine is the big expense, of course. Keurig’s stated $499.99 launch offer includes four boxes of AltaRounds. Choosing two Single Shot boxes and two Double Shot boxes would cover the coffee for your first 16 three-shot lattes.

Counting the starter coffee and the ingredients consumed, the total cost including the machine works out cheaper than my $9.53 order after 73 lattes made at home, or 70 with a subscription. That’s about two and a half months if you replace one purchased latte every day, or 14 to 15 weeks if you replace five a week.
After a year of daily use, each latte would average about $4.50 including the machine, coffee and milk, or $4.14 with a subscription. That is a considerable saving against my $9.53 order.

My receipt is doing some work here. If your usual latte costs $6, the same regular-price calculation takes about 167 replaced drinks to break even. And if you keep buying your usual coffee shop drink, the Alta becomes another coffee expense. It only earns back the purchase price through drinks you would otherwise have bought.
Alternatives to consider

If the Alta’s price is the sticking point, Lavazza’s Tablì Espresso Machine is listed at $129.99. It makes espresso, lungo and double espresso using compressed coffee tabs without a capsule. You’ll need a separate frother for milk drinks, and it only accepts Tablì Tabs. With both water tanks attached, the Tablì we measured was about four inches shallower than the Alta.

If you mostly drink drip coffee and want a plastic-free brew path, consider Caraway’s 10-Cup Coffee Maker, which launched at $495. Its water reservoir and carafe are glass, and its water path and brew basket are stainless steel. It uses your own grounds to brew two to 10 cups. It won’t make espresso, but it takes up considerably less counter depth in our measurements.
Frequently asked questions
Yes, the Alta accepts regular K-Cup pods as well as AltaRounds. You can keep using coffees you already buy in the K-Cup format.
No. AltaRounds are designed exclusively for the Alta brewer. You’ll need the Alta to use the new rounds.
Yes, according to Keurig, which says the rounds are BPI-certified for home and commercial composting. That claim applies to the rounds themselves, not their foil-based wrappers.
Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m Becca Delman, NBC Selected contributor and senior product manager for NBCUniversal News Group Commerce. For this review, I spent three weeks testing the Alta with other Selected staffers, concentrating on the espresso drinks I normally buy at coffee shops. We compared taste, counter space, milk-frothing noise and the handling of used rounds, and I calculated the cost against my own latte order.

title: Is a water leak detector worth it? Here’s what home experts say
summary: I reached out to home experts to learn more about water leak detectors and exactly how they work. Here’s how you can use them to avoid frozen pipes.
story: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends (and questions) on our timelines, like whether bath sheets are actually different from towels.

It’s expected that homeowners have things like smoke and carbon monoxide detectors in their homes to keep them and their families safe. But another type of home-related detector that’s also worth considering is a water leak detector. Depending on where you live and what type of home you have, a water leak detector can be a very beneficial tool, since it can help track water pressure and temperature, and help you get ahead of frozen pipes in the winter, which can be a major inconvenience — and a costly one if the pipes burst.

To learn more about how water leak detectors actually work and how to shop for one, I spoke to Lou Manfredini, a seasoned home expert at Ace Hardware*, who says that there are several different types of detectors to consider.

This water leak detector from Moen monitors both water floor and temperature in the water going through the pipes in your home’s water supply. Similar to the Hydrific detector, it attaches to the pipe and can send an alert straight to your phone via Moen’s Smart Water Network app. It also detects temperature changes in water (not just flow), so it can help prevent your pipes from freezing by turning off the water if the temperature drops below a certain degree. While you can technically install it yourself, the brand recommends having a professional do it.
How do water leak detectors work?

Water leak detectors, also sometimes called water leak sensors (which are technically a different type of detector), are systems that monitor water activity in your home. “There are several types, but basically they sense when water is present and will sound an alarm or send you a notification to your phone or computer to alert you of a leak,” says Manfredini. “The basic leak detectors are placed in areas where there may be a concern for water leaking.”

This includes areas like under a sink, under a water heater or in a basement, according to Manfredini. He further explains that they essentially watch for what seems like an excessive use of water, which can sometimes be caused by a burst pipe or a running toilet.

If it’s a point-of-use detector, it can literally sense when water is dripping on it or if it’s pooling around the device on the floor or the surface of a cabinet under a faucet for example. An in-line water detector connects to your pipes to determine changes in flow and temperature (more on this below).
What are the different types of water leak detectors?

There are a few different types of water leak detectors, but in general, you’ll find that many come in one of two forms, according to Chris Petri, owner of Petri Plumbing, Heating, Cooling & Drain Cleaning. These are the types you typically see:

Point-of-use water leak detectors: These types of water leak detectors literally sense water that is flooding around them. They’re commonly placed under a sink or water heater, according to Manfredini, and they will sound an alarm if they come in contact with water droplets or water pooling around them. Brands like Moen and GoveeLife have point-of-use water leak detectors. These types of detectors are usually circular or oblong in shape and adhere to a flat surface under a water source. Some water leak sensors include a power cable you place on the floor that will detect if water has already started to pool around it or if it’s submerged in water. You can use these types of sensors residentially or commercially, according to Manfredini.

Point-of-use water leak detectors: These types of water leak detectors literally sense water that is flooding around them. They’re commonly placed under a sink or water heater, according to Manfredini, and they will sound an alarm if they come in contact with water droplets or water pooling around them. Brands like Moen and GoveeLife have point-of-use water leak detectors. These types of detectors are usually circular or oblong in shape and adhere to a flat surface under a water source. Some water leak sensors include a power cable you place on the floor that will detect if water has already started to pool around it or if it’s submerged in water. You can use these types of sensors residentially or commercially, according to Manfredini.

In-line water leak detectors: “These are installed directly into your water main and use an internal turbine to measure water flow,” says Petri. “The device learns your home’s normal usage patterns—such as flow rate, duration, and volume.” If it detects a change in flow of your water (some also detect change in temperature), it will send you an alert and can automatically shut off the flow of water to prevent any flooding or freezing of pipes. This is also how a water leak detector can help prevent pipes from freezing, since some of them also monitor temperature. What’s also great about these types of detectors is that you don’t actually have to wait for it to start flooding or for it to touch water for it to alert you, according to Petri. The Moen Flo Smart Water Leak Detection Alarm is an example of this type.

In-line water leak detectors: “These are installed directly into your water main and use an internal turbine to measure water flow,” says Petri. “The device learns your home’s normal usage patterns—such as flow rate, duration, and volume.” If it detects a change in flow of your water (some also detect change in temperature), it will send you an alert and can automatically shut off the flow of water to prevent any flooding or freezing of pipes. This is also how a water leak detector can help prevent pipes from freezing, since some of them also monitor temperature. What’s also great about these types of detectors is that you don’t actually have to wait for it to start flooding or for it to touch water for it to alert you, according to Petri. The Moen Flo Smart Water Leak Detection Alarm is an example of this type.
What should you consider before buying a water leak detector?

“Every home benefits from proactive leak detection,” says Petri. “Waiting until a leak is visually noticeable often means damage has already occurred, especially since leaks frequently happen in hidden areas or while you are away.”

Getting a water leak detector that works for your type of space is important in determining if it’s a worthy investment, so it needs to have certain features. “Key features to consider include automatic water shutoff capabilities, smart notifications (such as app alerts), placement requirements, and whether you need whole-home coverage (in-line) or targeted area protection (point-of-use).”

title: Hayden Panettiere’s death is ruled accidental as police close probe
summary: Panettiere, 36, died of the toxic effects of multiple drugs, including fentanyl, the coroner determined.
story: Actor Hayden Panettiere’s death has been ruled an accident and the case is now closed, police in South Carolina announced Wednesday.

“Based on the Medical Examiner’s determination and the findings of the investigation, Hayden Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental,” Greenville police said, noting the investigation has concluded.
Panettiere, 36, the actor who starred in the shows “Heroes” and “Nashville,” was found unresponsive on Aug. 16 in a South Carolina apartment complex where she was staying.
Last month, the Greenville County Coroner’s Office ruled her death an accident caused by the toxic effects of multiple drugs: fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine.
The coroner said there were no signs of trauma that would have contributed to her death. Police also have said no signs of foul play were found during the initial response and investigation.
Panettiere, who had publicly discussed her struggle with addiction, had been in rehab just weeks before, according to the coroner’s report.

Panettiere’s on-again, off-again boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, was at the apartment complex at the time of her death. He showed police a “bag of medication” he said she was taking at the time, according to the police report.

After the coroner’s report was issued, Panettiere’s mother, Lesley Vogel, called her daughter a “fighter” who was “transparent with her addictions and her numerous rehab attempts show her resolve to live a healthy life.”
Vogel also said at the time that she had “never heard Hayden speak of fentanyl.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The Drug Enforcement Administration was also investigating, a source familiar with the probe previously told NBC News. The agency typically looks into the narcotics involved in a case, how they were obtained and whether any laws were broken in procuring the drugs.
Panettiere entered Hollywood as a child actor and later carved her own path, starring in the films “Remember the Titans,” “Ice Princess” and “Bring It On: All or Nothing.”

In her memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” she detailed how her life began to spiral after she had a daughter with Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko in 2014. She began drinking heavily to cope with postpartum depression and Klitschko’s distance, she wrote in the book.
She checked into rehab and gave Klitschko custody of their child in 2018.
In the book, she also discussed grappling with pain and grief after her brother, Jansen Panettiere, died in 2023 from an undiagnosed heart condition.

If you or someone you know is struggling with a drug or substance abuse problem, call these numbers for help: The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration’s national helpline is 1-800-662-HELP (1-800-662-4357); the National Drug Helpline is 1-844-289-0879; and the American Addiction Centers’ hotline is (866) 464-3073.

title: Ex-fiancé in ‘The People’s Court’ disappearance charged with murder after phone data review
summary: Dale Smith Jr., of Orlando, Florida, was arrested this month and charged with the second-degree murder of Michelle Parker.
story: A fresh look at cellphone data and text messages led to the arrest of a Florida man accused of murdering his ex-fiancée within hours of taping an episode for “The People’s Court” in 2011, court documents unsealed Tuesday revealed.
Dale Smith Jr., a 55-year-old Orlando resident, was taken into custody Oct. 14 and charged with second-degree murder in the death of Michelle Parker, whose body has never been found, police said.
Smith was 40 and Parker 33 when she was last seen alive on Nov. 17, 2011, the day the episode was taped. The two shared custody of twins at the time.

That afternoon, at about 2 p.m., Parker and Smith appeared for a taping of “The People’s Court” to settle a dispute over a $5,000 engagement ring she allegedly threw off a balcony. The judge ruled “that both parties were responsible for the ring and ordered they split the $5,000.00 damage,” according to an arrest warrant affidavit.
Smith told investigators that, after the taping of the show, Parker dropped the children off at his home and left about 10 minutes later, police said.
But surveillance cameras appeared to show that “the victim’s Hummer was at the suspect’s residence for at least one hour,” according to the affidavit.

Surveillance cameras showed Parker arriving at Smith’s building at about 3:18 p.m., according to the affidavit. At about 4:18 p.m. “victim and suspect phones leaves suspect’s home,” the document said.

By 4:32 p.m., the “victim’s and suspect’s phones continue moving west,” the affidavit said, a route that conflicted with Parker’s plans. “The victim was to travel north to pick up her oldest son who was waiting for her,” it said.

Parker’s brother, Dustin Erickson, also texted her that afternoon asking where she was. Her phone replied, “Waterford,” according to the affidavit. “Waterford” is the common local name for the Waterford Lakes Town Center shopping mall, about 12 miles northeast of Smith’s home.

“The victim’s cell phone never travels east or north towards the Waterford Lakes shopping center,” the affidavit said. “According to Dustin Erickson, the victim had no reason to deceive Dustin as to her location.”

Smith has previously said he had no idea where Parker went after dropping off the children. He told investigators he thought she was “laying low” after the “People’s Court” episode aired, the affidavit said.
“He wanted the victim to come home safe for their kids. However, according to his phone records, he never called or messaged her ever again after November 17, 2011,” the document said.
Police said Smith has a history of domestic violence. Detectives interviewed Jill Van Mechelen, another of his ex-fiancées, whom he knew before he met Parker.

“According to Jill Van Mechelen, the suspect would manually choke (strangle) her during these episodes of domestic physical violence,” the affidavit said. “The suspect also made threats to kill Jill Van Mechelen and her father. Jill Van Mechelen reported that the suspect told her on multiple occasions that he would kill her and/or her father and make them disappear.”
Smith’s attorney declined comment Wednesday, citing a court gag order.

title: Conservative influencer James O’Keefe charged with unlawful voting and identity theft in Minnesota
summary: O’Keefe was charged alongside fellow influencer Cam Higby. They are accused of misrepresenting themselves at polling places during Minnesota’s primary in August.
story: A Minnesota prosecutor charged conservative provocateur James O’Keefe and influencer Cam Higby on Wednesday with felony counts of unlawful voting and identity theft after they showed up at polling places in August using the names of registered voters.

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty, who announced the charges at a news conference, accused the pair of entering polling places during state primary election voting on Aug. 11 and identifying themselves using the names of registered voters in those precincts without those voters’ knowledge or permission.
Influencer James O’Keefe charged with unlawful voting

“Both men stopped short of signing the oath we all sign before receiving our ballot,” she said. “But Minnesota law states clearly that no individual shall intentionally misrepresent their identity in applying for a ballot.”

O’Keefe and Higby were using a process under Minnesota law known as vouching. It allows people to vouch for other voters on Election Day. A registered voter who lives in the same precinct can vouch for up to eight voters, while staff members of residential facilities can vouch for their residents.

The pair of influencers disguised and recorded themselves going undercover using hidden cameras at the polling places. They posted videos capturing their interactions on social media in August. O’Keefe said on X that they dressed in “Muslim garb” — including, for one of them, a full-face veil known as a niqab — and that their goal was to “expose the sheer lunacy of Minnesota’s ‘vouching’ system.”
Moriarty said Wednesday the office of Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon alerted her office to their conduct.

After O’Keefe and Higby’s videos became public in August, Simon said in a statement that their “apparent goal was to cast doubt on one or more Minnesota election laws that have been in force for over fifty years. Instead, they revealed their ignorance of how those laws actually work — while putting themselves in legal jeopardy.”
“The misconduct by this group is outrageous and totally unacceptable,” Simon added. “We have zero tolerance for lying, lawbreaking, and disruptions at our polling places.”

Police interviewed the registered voters whose names O’Keefe and Higby used, said Moriarty, who added that they also used the names of deceased voters. Asked where they obtained those names, Moriarty said, “We don’t know that.”
Moriarty said that they are not in jail and that instead, they will be issued summonses to appear in court in Minnesota.
Neither O’Keefe nor Higby immediately responded to requests for comment.

President Donald Trump has alleged for years that Democrats have committed voter fraud or have rigged elections against him. As part of those efforts to crack down on and prevent purported voter fraud, the Trump administration has been targeting Democratic-controlled states by trying to obtain state voter roll lists and identifying alleged noncitizen voters.

O’Keefe has been involved in other voter fraud-related incidents. In 2024, he and Project Veritas, which he founded, settled a lawsuit brought by a Pennsylvania postmaster after the group promoted a postal worker’s false claims of voter fraud during the 2020 presidential election. O’Keefe was removed as the head of Project Veritas in 2023.
Higby was a journalist for conservative outlets and now operates a YouTube account with 285,000 subscribers.

title: Jimmy Fallon and Jamie Lee Curtis’ Shot-for-Shot Remake of ‘You Can See Everything’ Needs an Emmy, Fans Say
summary: Jimmy Fallon and Jamie Lee Curtis’ recreated “You Can See Everything” and the clip went viral. See the moment and fans’ responses.
story: “You Can See Everything” has taken the box office — and late-night television — by storm.

The Oct. 28 episode of “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon” featured Fallon and guest Jamie Lee Curtis doing a shot-by-shot remake of Elizabeth Holmes and director Nathan Fielder’s intense scene in “You Can See Everything.”
“Now, be honest. Do you really want to be on the show tonight?” asked Fallon, with expressions eerily similar to Fielder’s, while tense music played underneath.
The camera then panned to Curtis, whose eyes stayed wide open, just like Holmes’ did in the scene in the movie.
“Of course I do. I love talking to you,” she replied.
“So, you’re not just here to promote your new show, ‘Newlyweds?’” he asked, alluding to her NBC sitcom.
“No. I’m engaging with you as a human being. ... Why would I deceive you? There’s no reason for me to do that,” she replied, repeating Holmes’ same lines from the scene in the documentary.
Fallon continued to mimic Fielder’s reaction from the movie, right down to slightly moving his tongue before he asked, like Fielder did, if Curtis is “being real right now.”
“I’m always being real,” Curtis replied, echoing Holmes’ line.
Fallon then said he’ll see her on the show and walked away before the music stopped and Curtis broke character.
The sketch quickly went viral, with fans on Instagram raving about how good it was.
“DAMN, give the Emmy to Jimmy for this sketch,” someone wrote.
“How are they both so good, it’s just a sketch,” someone else commented.
“Truly Excellent!!” gushed Oscar nominee Naomi Watts.
“Genuinely thought this actually was Fielder,” another person wrote.
“Give this makeup artist a raise,” one fan chimed in.
Even the TODAY crew was blown away.
“That’s distracting, it’s so good,” Carson Daly said Oct. 29 on the show.
“Its’s dead on. Jimmy should win an Emmy for that portrayal,” Savannah Guthrie said.

“You Can See Everything” chronicles the time leading up to Holmes, founder and CEO of healthcare company Theranos, serving her prison sentence after being convicted of four federal charges of wire fraud in 2022.

The nearly three-hour film has been a box office smash, earning $15 million in its debut weekend, the biggest tally in an opening weekend for a non-music documentary since Michael Moore’s 2004 documentary, “Fahrenheit 9/11.”

title: ‘Love Island USA’ Stars, Including Zach, Cheer on Kayda as She Closes Runway Show
summary: Kayda Bosse felt the love as she closed out the True Religion x Baby Phat runway show, while beau Zach Georgiou and Aniya Harvey cheered her on.
story: Kayda Bosse felt the love as she closed out the True Religion x Baby Phat runway show.
The “Love Island USA” Season 8 star strutted in a matching denim two-piece set, trimmed with faux fur as the brands celebrated their first-ever collaboration on Oct. 28 in Van Nuy, California.
The reality star-turned-model had her own cheering squad in the front row, which included beau Zach Georgiou, proving that they’re still going strong.
Also in attendance was Zach’s brother and fellow “Love Island USA” alum Charlie Georgiou, as well as Season 7’s Clarke Carraway and Season 6’s Sierra Mills.
Aniya Harvey, who also appeared on the same season as Kayda and Zach, was seen in the stands. She twinned with the same look that her fellow Islander wore.
During the runway show, Yume performed as the models showed off the collection. When it was Kayda’s turn to conclude the presentation, Zach was seen with his phone out and recording her.
The crowd and her friends cheered as she walked past them. Kayda smiled wide and stretched out her hand to Zach.
He posted video from his point of view on his Instagram story, adding a heart eye emoji.
It appears the couple, who came in fourth place, are still enjoying each other’s company. Just days before her fashion-filled moment, Kayda celebrated Zach’s birthday with a heartfelt post.

“To the guy I can be my truest self around,” she captioned a slideshow with photos of the two. “Your humor is one of the things I cherish most about you. You always find a way to make me smile in any situation. You have such a genuine way about you. I admire the person you are.”
She added that she hoped the “next chapter of your life brings you as much happiness as you bring to the people around you. Happy birthday Zacharias.”
In the comments, he replied, “Thankyou bby girl,” adding a red heart.

title: What Mel Robbins Makes of the ‘Make Them’ Theory In ‘Nobody Wants This’
summary: Mel Robbins has seen Nobody Wants This and heard of the Make Them theory. Here’s her response.
story: Mel Robbins has heard of the “make them” theory. In fact, she says she’s been trying it for years.
And it “does not work,” she tells TODAY.com backstage at Studio 1A Oct. 28.

In this season of “Nobody Wants This,” Morgan (Justine Lupe) goes viral for a solo episode of the podcast she usually co-hosts with her sister, Joanne (Kristen Bell). Riffing on Robbins’ “let them” theory, she proposes an alternative: Make them.

“Let them,” which is also the name of Robbins’ blockbuster book, is a type of surrender based on stoicism and ancient philosophy, Robbins says. In a previous interview with TODAY.com, she said the concept allows you to “see people exactly as they are instead of stressing yourself out wishing they were different.”
Morgan’s “make them” theory is exactly that opposite. Rather than let people do what they want, you make them do as you want.
Robbins watched “Nobody Wants This” and was moved by the apparent reference, because she says it’s proof her book is now “part of culture.”
Below, Robbins unpacks “make them” vs. “let them,” her new People Magazine cover and whether her three kids take her famous advice in conversation with TODAY.com.

I have used the “make them” method for 54 years. I have tried to make them do the dishes, make them lose weight, make them change their mind, make them go to therapy, make them do their homework, and that does not work. What ends up happening when you try to make somebody change is they resist the thing you’re making them do.

I think it’s amazing and fun and funny, but it’s the way we’re all going through life right now, which is why we’re all so stressed out and why we’re all frustrated in our relationships and with other people.

I find it’s much more strategic to work with the neuroscience, and just let people have the dignity of their own experience. Let people reveal who they are to you, and let them see your example. A funny thing happens, and this isn’t my theory, it’s actual hard science. When somebody has the space to sit with themselves, and when somebody does not feel pressured to change, they suddenly believe it’s their idea. They suddenly have room to step toward the things that you’ve been b----- about forever, because nobody wants to be told, “I told you so.”

I love the show, and I love everybody on it, and I was super flattered. I have created a simple theory that explains stoicism and radical acceptance and Buddhism and the serenity prayer, because that’s what the “let them” theory is.

When you see people not only apply it, but it becomes part of culture ... you see people make jokes about it — you know you have shared something that is of value. If it’s something simple, if it works, if it’s sticky, so people can remember it, that’s what makes for a really good idea.

No, absolutely not. I’m their mother. Why would they listen to me? They are biologically engineered to argue against and resist everything I try to make them do. I have learned the single best piece of advice in my 50s that I wish I had had when I was born, and it’s this. Every parent should just repeat this sentence: Do you want my advice, or do you just want me to listen? Ninety-nine percent of the time, your children and everybody in your life just wants you to listen.
But no, my children don’t listen to me.

You cannot tell somebody the lesson they have to learn by failing or experiencing the pain of doing it your way. You just can’t. Some lessons cannot be transferred through language. They have to be learned through experience.
As moms in particular, we’re trying to prevent you from experiencing the pain that we’ve experienced. The irony is, the exact pain you need to learn the lesson, we can’t teach.
We’re a couple days away from Halloween right now. It feels like I’m in a costume. I’ve never imagined a moment where I would be on the cover of People.

To see something this big happen in my career, and to know that it’s happening because of all of the work that I did to change myself and become a person that is someone that I’m proud of, and then just sharing what I’m learning to be celebrated for the work that we can all do to change our lives — that’s incredible.

I’m just very proud. I’m so happy that the 41-year-old depressed, insecure, jealous, loser version of me got herself together and decided that she was worth working on, and her life was worth making better. Inside each of us, there is the desire to thrive. There is the desire to contribute. There is the desire to be happy. And I hope, in some small way, that this article and seeing how far one person can come in their life in 15, 16 years, and the positive difference that you can make — I hope it inspires somebody to make a decision to make their life better while they can.

I woke up dumb every day. Really dumb. If you think about it, if you’re really honest with yourself, there are things that you’re doing right now that are dumb, and they’re embarrassing. If you really stop and say, “OK, I can do better. I can take better care of myself. I can learn how to have a positive attitude. I don’t have to hang out with negative idiots. ... The time I’m spending complaining and feeling sorry for myself is time I could actually invest in changing my mindset and my habits.”

When you do that, you immediately become a different person. The results take time, but you start to feel differently the moment you act differently. I think that’s what shocked me the most. I stayed miserable for a long time. It’s pretty surprising how different and how much better you can feel in a very short period of time simply by changing how you act every day.

title: Elizabeth Holmes Told TODAY in 2016 She Had ‘No Doubt’ Her Company Would Survive
summary: Elizabeth Holmes spoke with TODAY in 2016 amid accusations that her Theranos technology was faulty.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment features Eliazbeth Holmes being interviewed in 2016.

Elizabeth Holmes has once again found herself in the public eye, thanks to the film “You Can See Everything.” The documentary, which follows her weeks before she begins her prison sentence, earned $15 million in its opening weekend earlier this month, the most for a debut weekend for a non-music doc since Michael Moore’s 2004 movie, “Fahrenheit 9/11.”

Holmes is the founder and former CEO of Theranos, a company that sought to revolutionize blood testing, partnering with Walgreens to offer fast in-store blood tests for more than 20 diseases at a cheaper price than what they traditionally cost, due to secret technology. Holmes raised nearly $1 billion and the company was once valued at $9 billion, bringing her wealth and fame among the Silicon Valley set.

Accusations, however, came out that Theranos’ technology was faulty and Holmes was convicted in 2022 of four federal charges of wire fraud for misrepresenting to investors what the Theranos technology could do.
In 2016, then-NBC special anchor Maria Shriver sat down with Holmes to discuss the questions that emerged about her product’s accuracy.
Elizabeth Holmes Defended Theranos

After reports began circulating about the methods Theranos used, Holmes discussed her company in an interview that aired April 16, 2016, in which she opened up about the growing controversy over her company.
“I’m a better person for it, and I’m a better leader,” she said.
Holmes defended Theranos and the blood testing methods it used.
“It’s affordable,” she said. “That means it’s transparent in terms of pricing. That means that it’s available to people as a basic right, early, before they’re sick.”
What Did Elizabeth Holmes Say About the Negative Reports?
In 2015, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services found multiple violations at one of Holmes’ labs which presented a threat to the safety of patients.
“I feel devastated that we did not catch and fix these issues faster,” she said.
Holmes said the buck has to stop with her.

“I’m the founder and CEO of this company. Anything that happens in this company is my responsibility,” she said. “At the end of the day, we stop testing and have taken the approach of saying, ‘Let’s rebuild this entire laboratory from scratch, so that we can ensure it never happens again.’”
Elizabeth Holmes Believed in the Future of Theranos
Holmes said she thought the correct policies were in place, but added she was “absolutely” sure Theranos would withstand all its issues and survive.
“No doubt. I know what we’ve built, and I know what we’ve created, and I know what it means to people, and it is a change that needs to happen in the world,” she said.

title: ‘Wicker’ Had the Internet Thirsting, But Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård Say the Film Is About More Than Lust
summary: Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård explained the ending of “Wicker” and how their characters went from lust to love.
story: Spoilers ahead for “Wicker” starring Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård.

When the trailer for “Wicker” was released, the internet began thirsting over Alexander Skarsgård’s willow-woven leading man. That’s because the NSFW teaser featured the actor alongside Olivia Colman getting, well, down and dirty and breaking beds to the shock of the townspeople and viewers.

But the film is more than just a satirical comedy about sex with a wickedly handsome wicker man. Instead, it shows the intimacy, vulnerability and trust required to open one’s heart to love. Its emotional ending proves that despite the challenges in marriages and the outside noise, love conquers all.

“It’s a beautiful love story that’s funny and irreverent, but set in a fantastical world that (Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson), our writers, directors, created with extraordinary collaborators,” Skarsgård tells TODAY.com. “But with a lot of social commentary about patriarchy and social hierarchy and the institution of marriage, but done with so much levity and a light touch.”
What Is ‘Wicker’ About?

“Wicker,” out now, stars Colman as an independent yet lonely Fisherwoman, constantly ostracized by villagers. When asked if she’s “caught herself a lover,” she says, “Love seems more burden than a prize.”

But when the Fisherwoman has a change of heart, she requests the local Basketmaker (Peter Dinklage) to make her a husband. Woven from willow with broad-shoulders, strong arms and incredible, umm, assets, the wicker man is “gentle-spoken and utterly devoted.” That’s how author Ursula Wills describes him in her short story “The Wicker Husband,” which the movie is based on.

“I love her and admire her,” Colman tells TODAY.com of her character. “She has strengths in her solitude and she’s got her own agency, and she’s amazing. But she has armor. She’s been mocked her whole life and she ignores it, which is admirable. But at some point she did go, ‘I’ve had enough. I’m going to have the last laugh.’”
What the Fisherwoman doesn’t realize, Colman says, is “that she’s going to fall in love.”

That journey rocks Fisherwoman, and the townsfolk, to the core. As she opens herself up to love — “it’s terrifying doing that,” she says — she also faces more scrutiny and jealousy from those around her.

“It’s lust, initially, isn’t it?” Colman says about the early relationship between Fisherwoman and her Wicker Husband, adding that her character does eventually “fall in love with someone who’s marvelous.”
“They learn about love together,” she says.
Skarsgård brings to light one of the Fisherwoman’s most intimate quotes from the film to showcase her journey.

“Fisherwoman tells the Wicker Husband, ‘You have my heart now,’ and that’s what’s scary about it. Your heart is in someone else’s hands, and your happiness is in their hands,” Skarsgård says. “There’s a lot of beauty in that, but it’s also scary because you know that you can get hurt.”
Having been on her own her whole life, Colman says Fisherwoman’s relationship with Wicker Husband goes from lust to love when she realizes he’s someone she can lean on.
The turning point begins when one morning, after a night of enjoying their marriage, the Wicker Husband says, “The bed is broken. Bring me a hammer. I will fix it.”
“Their days are nicer when they’re together. They enhance each other rather than take from each other,” Colman says.
How Does ‘Wicker’ End?

Their marriage, however, makes the townspeople insecure, questioning their own marriages. The women see how Wicker Husband is so attentive, caring and goes out of his way to make Fisherwoman’s life better. The husbands feel threatened and angry towards Wicker Husband for highlighting their faults.

Their relationship irritates the Tailor’s Wife (Elizabeth Debicki) the most. The queen bee of the town, Tailor’s Wife seemingly has it all: a hard working husband and wonderful children. But she’s a homemaker with dreams of having her own identity.

She envies Fisherwoman’s independence and how she has a supportive partner. So when her sister’s husband dies and the young widow asks the Basketmaker to weave her a baby, the Tailor’s Wife devises a plan to separate Fisherwoman and Wicker Husband.

The Tailor’s Wife implies that Wicker Husband has been unfaithful. Fisherwoman gets caught up in the lies and rumors, and when she sees the Wicker Baby, she becomes completely distraught. She believes her loyal husband has betrayed her, which he has not.

“Mourning is the price we pay for love. So unfortunately, if you love deeply, it’s going to feel awful when it’s not there,” Colman says. “But would you ever say no to the love in the first place? I wouldn’t. It’s a terrible leap of faith, but worth doing.”
What happens next shows viewers how it’s easier to believe the bad than the good, one of the film’s themes. The Fisherwoman throws fire on her delicate partner, who runs away engulfed in flames.
“Not her finest hour, definitely,” quips Colman.
Heartbroken, she attempts to continue her life as before. But love has changed her, and losing that love has destroyed her.

When Basketmaker finds a badly burned and almost destroyed Wicker Husband in the woods, he mends him. The Tailor Wife’s Sister, meanwhile, has had a mental breakdown and has abandoned her Wicker Baby, only to be found by Fisherwoman.
When Basketmaker sees the Fisherwoman, he reminds her that Wicker Husbands can’t have Wicker Babies, implying that her adoring spouse did not cheat.

In the end, in an act of revenge, Basketmaker shakes up the town by offering a Wicker Wife to the highest bidder. The villagers show their true and disgusting colors, showing the craftsman the lengths they will go to to have their own serviceable companion. However, the Wicker Wife is made of blackthorn, a thorny shrub, and the (un)lucky winner appears to be mutilated by his new beloved when she goes in for a kiss.

As for the Fisherwoman, she is reunited with her Wicker Husband, who reminds her that she is the only one for him. With their adopted Wicker Baby, they decide to leave town and start a new life together away from the spiteful townspeople.

title: Wynonna Judd Says She Plans to Visit Estranged Daughter Grace
summary: Wynonna Judd isn’t giving up hope of repairing her relationship with her estranged daughter, Grace Kelley. She reveals plans to visit her in prison to Hoda Kotb in an episode of Making Space.
story: Wynonna Judd isn’t giving up hope of repairing her relationship with her estranged daughter, Grace Kelley.

In a candid conversation with Hoda Kotb on the Oct. 28 episode of the “Making Space” podcast, the country music star revealed that she plans to visit her daughter again — and made it clear that no matter how much time passes, she’ll never stop hoping for a relationship.
When asked if reconciliation is possible, Judd replied without hesitation: “Absolutely.”
“I’m going to go see her at some point,” she added. “I’m going to do it with as much presence as I can in this situation.”
Judd went on to explain that she used to visit Kelley every week in prison, which inspired the song “Drive” on her new album, “The Hard Truth,” released Oct. 2, 2026.

Kelley has struggled with addiction and legal troubles over the years and is currently serving a 15-month sentence at a Virginia jail after pleading guilty to driving with a suspended or revoked license in June 2026.
Judd said that they became estranged after she stopped providing financial support.

“I bought her five cars, and I gave her money for food and shelter, and yet she spent it on drugs. I can’t stop that, but I can say no,” she told Kotb. “Once the money ran out, she did too. She cut me off.”
Kotb asked whether Judd feels guilty about the situation.
“Every day,” Judd answered. “I carry it because I think, what could I have done differently?”
She reflected on raising her children while touring at the height of her career and wondered whether she should have taken more time off.
“I think it’s the hardest thing I’ve ever done,” Judd told Kotb. “I don’t know how in the world I’m doing it at times. Letting go of my daughter, letting her find her way.”
“I miss her, and I want her back,” she said.
Kotb asked Judd what she would say to other parents who are estranged from their children.
“Never give up on them. They’re alive,” she said.
She explained that she’s ready if Kelley wants to return to her life, but that she also needs to maintain the boundaries she has set.

“I’m devastated, but I also know that she’s got to figure it out for herself,” she said. “If Grace wants back into my life, I’m ready, and I love her dearly. I miss her every second of every breath that I take as a mom.”
“I am going to be one of those that will die hoping”

title: ‘DWTS’ Horror Movie Night Shocks Fans With Shirley Ballas’ Brutal Scores, Double Elimination
summary: See the scores and who got eliminated during the “DWTS” Horror Movie Night episode of Oct. 27.
story: Spooky season was officially in session on “Dancing With the Stars.”
The Tuesday, Oct. 27, episode brought out killer choreography for Horror Movie Night, where the remaining 10 couples performed routines inspired by legendary horror films.
After last week’s Dedication Night ended with no elimination, the pairs had to work twice as hard to avoid being cut from the competition.
After an eerie opening number by the eliminated pros, co-hosts Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough kicked off the show, which also saw the return of Val Chmerkovskiy after his one week suspension.
Joining Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough this week as guest judge was “Dancing with the Stars: The Next Pro” judge, and Mark Ballas’ mom, Shirley Ballas.
Read all about what went down during the Oct. 27 episode of “DWTS,” including the dances and scores of each couple.

Julia Stiles was up first with an Argentine tango, saying she felt defeated during rehearsals and pressured by partner Ezra Sosa. When they got on the ballroom floor, the results were mixed from judges who felt she held back. But it was Shirley Ballas who stunned the couple (and everyone else) when she gave them a 4 out of 10. Inaba and Derek Hough gave them a 7, while Tonioli dished out an 8.

When Harry Shum Jr. and partner Jenna Johnson performed their contemporary, they blew the judges, including Shirley Ballas away, who said she’d never seen anything like that before. But did her comments translate to her score? Yes, the couple got the first perfect score of the season.
The guest judge continued with tough criticisms when it came to Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik. She said it didn’t include enough paso doble content and gave them a 4 out of 10.

Contemporary proved to be a crowd pleaser during the night. Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold’s routine got the judges really excited, calling it his best performance yet. Jackson Olson and Emma Slater’s performance was also filled with action and great remarks.

When it came to judging her son and partner Maura Higgins, Shirley Ballas did not hold back. She was in tune with how her fellow judges felt, noting she enjoyed the lifts, believed it was powerful but to work on her feet.
After being suspended for since-deleted comments about Inaba’s critiques about a lift in wife Johnson’s routine during the Oct. 13 episode, the pro returned to dance with partner Jenna Dewan.
During rehearsals, Chmerkovskiy apologized for having to miss an episode. “We are back together. I am so sorry for all the chaos,” he told Dewan. “You did not sign up for that and I feel awful.”
